Two per cent of the entire configuration space makes money in the second half. If the edge were real and broad you would expect most of the 423 profitable cells to also be profitable in the back half; instead 423 shrinks to 36. With a 2% base rate you would expect about 8 of the 423 to clear the full bar by luck alone. Five did. The five "survivors" of the blanket sweep are exactly what chance hands you, and quoting any one of them would be a lie of selection.

But the halves test is confounded, and I checked

Before accepting "the edge decayed", I looked at what the two halves actually are.

halfdatessessionsATR20 medianmean daily range|15-min move| p90ER30 median
first07-16 → 08-041413.9pt709pt67.1pt0.172
second08-05 → 08-24149.3pt398pt44.4pt0.156

The second half is a 33% quieter tape by ATR and 44% quieter by daily range. So "it stopped working in half two" and "it stops working when volatility halves" are the same sentence, and the blanket halves test cannot tell them apart. That is precisely the failure mode the desk's own backtest discipline warns about — a blanket cross-tape number averages the regimes a config should be ON with those it should be OFF, and is a bug. So I split by regime first.

3. STEP THREE — THE FILTER, AND THE ONE THAT ACTUALLY WORKED
Regime first, config second

I bucketed every board by the ATR level at entry — causal, known before the trade, and the live router's own meter — and re-ran a 216-cell entry × exit sweep inside each bucket, requiring both halves of that bucket to be positive.

ATR20 at entrycells scorednet > 02nd half > 0pass both halves + strip-3
ATR < 9 (quiet / dead)21623 (11%)15 (7%)4 (2%)
ATR 9–14 (the desk's normal tape)216188 (87%)75 (35%)66 (31%)
ATR ≥ 14 (violent)21681 (38%)39 (18%)16 (7%)

A fifteen-fold difference in survival rate between buckets is not something chance produces evenly. Something real lives in the middle band, and the blanket number had been averaging it away.

…but first, is that just leverage?

Stops and targets are ATR-scaled, so a higher-ATR trade is mechanically a bigger bet in dollars. If the "filter" simply selects bigger bets, dollars per trade rises while the actual edge stays flat, and the rule is a position-sizing choice dressed up as an insight. So I rescored everything in R — net P&L divided by (ATR at entry × $2) — which is the same trade measured in units of what it risked.

ATR20 bandW8 k2.5 (R/trade)W10 k2.5 (R/trade)W15 k3.0 (R/trade)agreement
0–7+0.07+0.45−0.12no
7–9+0.27−0.63−0.24no
9–11+0.48−0.38+0.26no
11–13+0.07+0.66+1.03partial
13–16+1.42+1.09+0.87all three
16+−0.11+0.19−0.11no (all ≈ 0)

In R the relationship is not monotone in ATR, which kills the leverage explanation. It is a band: the money is between roughly 11 and 16 points of ATR, and both edges matter. Below it the moves are too small relative to noise and the round trip; above it the tape is violent enough that a "proven" move is more often an exhausted one — which is the same thing the abs_veto rehab found when the amp_floor let through elevated-ATR-but-spent overnight thrusts.

The candidate
RIDER_ALL / board_atrband — sampled at each completed one-minute bar. ATR20 = mean 1-min high−low over the last 20 minutes. Fire when 11 ≤ ATR20 < 16 AND |net over 10 min| ≥ 2.5 × ATR20 AND ER(10 min) ≥ 0.50. Direction = sign of the 10-minute move. Stop 3.0 × ATR, target 6.0 × ATR, flat at 240 minutes, 60-minute lockout between fires.

Five neighbouring entry definitions, all between +$15.93 and +$24.37 a trade, all surviving strip-best-10, all positive in both halves. That is a parameter plateau, not a step. By this desk's stated bar — expectancy and robustness, never win rate — 44% winning is irrelevant and +0.9R a trade over 146 trades with strip-10 intact is a serious candidate.

The controls
controlresultreading
Direction flipped (same boards, opposite side)−$2,436, −$16.68/tr, −0.637Rdirection is doing real work — it is not an exit artefact
Random-time placebo — same ATR band, random minutes, random side, 400 drawsnull mean +$229, sd $1,335 → p = 0.0125beats a random entry with the same exit
Placebo cut — keep a random 146 of the 518 unfiltered fires, 4,000 drawsnull mean +$1,088, sd $1,246 → p = 0.029the ATR band beats discarding the same number of fires at random
Unfiltered (all ATR)518 trades, +$3,864, +$7.46/tr, +0.190Rthe band roughly triples expectancy per trade
★ What the cut COSTS — the number I am obliged to report and it is not flattering

Cutting to the ATR band discards 372 of the 518 fires. Those 372 contain 131 winners worth +$18,483 which we forgo, and 241 losers worth −$18,115 which we avoid. Net effect of the entire filter on the bottom line: +$368.

So the ATR band does not find money. It concentrates the same money into a quarter of the trades. That is genuinely worth something — it is what lifts $7.46 a trade to $23.95 and what makes the thing survive strip-10 — but anyone reading "+0.9R a trade" as "the filter found an edge" has it backwards. The filter found a smaller sample.

And the caveat I have to put next to my own p-values

I chose the band edges after looking at the data. There were roughly 36 plausible lo × hi combinations in the sweep I ran. A p of 0.029 against 36 looks, corrected, like a p of about 1.0. The placebo cut controls for "any cut of this size" but not for "I went looking for the best cut". The in-sample battery above is real and the controls are honest, but it is not, on its own, evidence that survives the multiplicity. Which is why the next section exists.

4. THE OUT-OF-SAMPLE LEG — AND THE KILL

The 5s lake is 28 sessions. The parquet lake also carries a one-minute backfill running back to 2025-09-14 — 295,845 bars, 236 sessions before the 5s tape even begins. Not one parameter above was chosen on it, and it is the best-powered test available to this desk.

Two honesty notes before the number. The exit has to be simulated on one-minute bars there, which is a coarser and more punishing ruler — inside a bar I still resolve stop-before-target, and the fill is a minute later. To measure how much coarseness costs, I ran the in-sample window through the coarse simulator too:

The coarse ruler reads roughly half. Keep that in mind and then read this:

legnsessionsnet $$/tradeR/trade95% CI on R/tradestrip-3strip-10half 1half 2day-green

Fourteen dollars. Over eleven months. Double it for the coarse ruler and it is twenty-eight dollars. Month by month it is a coin toss: +734, −84, +437, −1,510, −1,333, −555, +373, +496, +1,844, −669, +281 — six green months out of eleven. It does not survive stripping its three best trades.

The ATR band is not useless: without it the same entries lose $3,640 and −0.047R. The band takes the rider from clearly negative to exactly zero. That is a real filter doing real work on a mechanism that has no edge to protect.

Step Two, re-run properly on the big sample

The wide-exit sweep on 28 sessions was the underpowered version. Here it is on 236, on the banded entry set (n = 1,289), net $ / R per trade:

Forty-one of the 42 cells are negative or within noise of zero, and the five nominally positive ones are scattered, not clustered. +$1,367 sits directly beside −$576 and −$2,573. There is no plateau anywhere on this surface.

So: "an entry that only pays with a wide exit is a finding, not a failure" — I tested that properly, and for this entry it is a failure. The wide exit reliably makes the rider less negative (target 6.0 is the best column in every row) but it never makes it positive. That is not a refutation of the exhaustion_short rehab, which was a different gate's entries; it is a refutation of the hope that the same medicine cures this one.

Does the direction carry anything at all?

Yes, and this is the most useful salvage in the section. Re-simulating every board on the opposite side:

exitwith-trend (as designed)counter-trendseparation

A proven move genuinely does continue more often than it reverses — consistently, in every exit, across 1,289 out-of-sample trades. The information is real. It is worth about +0.06 to +0.11R a trade, and the round trip alone costs 0.06R at the band's midpoint. The edge exists and is roughly the same size as the toll booth. That is the honest shape of this whole problem.

One tick of slippage takes the all-day rider negative. And the power calculation: at the band midpoint 1R is $25 and the round trip is 0.060R; to establish a real expectancy of +0.10R a trade against what we actually measured would need roughly 10,500 trades, about eight years of this rider's fire rate. This is not a "needs more data" case. It is a "the effect is smaller than the measurement error and smaller than the costs" case.

The overnight lead dies on replication, and it dies on the controls rather than on the headline. The rider itself keeps its sign in both samples for one particular parameterisation. But the claim — that overnight tape behaves differently from daytime tape for a boarding rider — is not reproduced: on the held-out lake daytime is just as good or better in five of six comparisons, and the counter-trend control, which was reassuringly negative out of sample, comes back positive. When your control flips sign, you are reading noise.

Two further honesty points. The session split was one of three post-hoc comparisons, so its nominal significance should be trebled. And the random-time placebo inside the same band and the same session gives p = 0.097 — even on its own generating sample it is only about 1.3 standard deviations above firing at random times.

It is not nothing, and I am not calling it dead. It has the right sign in two independent samples, its counter-trend leg is negative in both, and it is the only thing in this study that survives a full point of slippage. That earns incubation, not deployment. See the disposition table.

7. THE STONE I HAD NOT TURNED — THE L2 BOOK AT THE BOARD MOMENT

The census scores every run for far-side depletion, and I had used none of it. The obvious question: at the moment the board rule fires, does a thin far side — the side price is running into — tell us which of those 34 daily fires is a real run? We hold 264 million MNQ book rows from 07-31 to 08-24, so this is answerable with data we already have.

For each of the 311 fires inside the book window I took the far-side share of level-1-to-3 depth over the 30 seconds before entry (below 0.50 = the far side is thin = the run is telegraphed).

far-side sharennet $$/tradeR/tradewin
0.00–0.4213−$38−$2.93−0.34331%
0.42–0.4744−$300−$6.82−0.54430%
0.47–0.50109−$680−$6.24−0.14235%
0.50–0.5389+$188+$2.11+0.13936%
0.53–0.5845−$379−$8.42−0.30833%
0.58–1.0111−$166−$15.09−0.66227%

A clean null. Correlation between far-side share and R is −0.009 across 311 trades. Cutting to a thin far side gives −0.265R against −0.060R for a thick one — i.e. the wrong way round — and against a random cut of the same size the placebo p is 0.62. There is no ordering, no monotonicity, no signal. The L2 book, read this way, at this moment, tells us nothing about which board becomes a run.

That closes the stone. It also means "we need a data source we do not capture" is not the excuse available here — we had the deepest data on the desk and it was empty.

8. STEP FIVE — SIZING THE PRIZE HONESTLY
$as % of the $9,610 sat-out ceiling
ORACLE — perfect late board (fires in 62/62 at a median 3 min), exit at the exact run terminus, no costs, cheats$5,09453%
ORACLE — the same, with a detector you would actually deploy (W=10, k=1.5, ER≥0.50)$2,28624%
ORACLE — with the candidate's own trigger (W=10, k=2.5, ER≥0.50)$1,91020%
CAUSAL — the candidate rider, one slot, run over the census week itself−$245−3%
CAUSAL — same rider, overnight only, census week−$214−2%
CAUSAL — same rider, one slot, whole 5s lake, scaled to a 5-session week+$433/weekin-sample only
CAUSAL — same rider, corrected by the 236-session out-of-sample leg≈ $0/week0%

On the census week itself, running one position at a time, the candidate took 42 trades and lost $245. It did show up — it participated in 32 of the 62 sat-out runs, roughly half — and it still lost money, because the other trades cost more than the runs paid. That is the sharpest single sentence in this report: showing up to half the runs was not the hard part, and it did not help.

The oracle table is the number to carry forward. This is a $2,000–$5,000-a-week oracle, not a $9,610-a-week one, and per the desk's own precedent that distinction changes what the money is worth building for. The gap between the $5,094 oracle and the $0 causal result is not an exit problem and not a detection problem — it is selection, and it is 100% of the gap.

Why the mechanism fails, in one paragraph. At the moment the boarding rule is true, the median run has 12 to 41 points left depending on how much confirmation you demand — and the same rule is true 34 times a day on tape that does nothing. The trades that are not runs pay the stop, which at 3×ATR in the 11–16 band is 33 to 48 points. So the rider is risking 33–48 points to collect a median 12–41, and it must be right far more often than 44% of the time for that to work. It is not. The wide exit helps because it lets the occasional big run pay for many stops, but the ratio of runs to non-runs at the moment of firing — about 1 in 20 — is simply too thin. Boarding is solved. Selecting is not. That is the same conclusion the greenfield census reached from the other end when it found that a plain 3/6×ATR exit converts 40% of the ceiling but 105 of 155 fires are not runs at all.

10. DISPOSITION
leadverdictwhy / what would revive it
rider_w5 (live shadow arm)REFUTEDNamed tests: 51 live forward trades at −$28.84/tr, red in all four ATR buckets; 1,339 OOS trades at −$5.43/tr with strip-3 at −$9,293; −$174 on the census week it was built for; and its in-sample +$1,936 collapses to +$282 on strip-best-3. Mechanism stated in §8: at fire time the median run has 12–41pt left against a 33–48pt stop, and only ~1 fire in 20 is a run. Action: retire the arm.
board_atrband (the candidate)PARKEDPassed every in-sample test including two placebos, then measured +$14 over 236 sessions. Revive only with a SELECTOR — something that predicts which board becomes a run. Not more days: the power calculation says ~10,500 trades to separate it from zero. The census's own finding points the way (size threshold, ≥120pt boarding), and that is a different study from this one.
board_overnightSHADOWRight sign in two independent samples (+0.444R and +0.224R), counter-trend leg negative in both, survives a full point of slippage. But its daytime and counter-trend controls reverse on the held-out sample and its placebo p is 0.097. Shadow it as an instrumented question, not as a candidate — the specific thing to buy is whether overnight boards really differ from daytime ones, which the two samples disagree about. Block and promotion bar below. Needs two small code changes first (§11).
board_wide / board_holdcap / board_blanketPARKEDAll failed as built on both-halves or the OOS sweep. Revive only if the selection problem is solved first — the exit was never the binding constraint here, which the 42-cell OOS surface establishes.
board_chandelierPARKED, not refutedIt was never honestly tested — the trail was broken. With the corrected trail it is negative everywhere, but the shape (wide stop + armed trail) is what grind_long's deployed pure-6.0 chandelier runs on, so the mechanism is not disproven, only this application of it. Revive on a selected entry set, never on this unselected one.
board_book (L2 far-side depletion as selector)REFUTEDNamed test: 311 fires against 264M book rows, correlation −0.009, no monotone band, placebo p=0.62. No reformulation of this measurement (far-side share, 3 deep, 30s pre-entry) survives; a different book statistic — resting-size decay rate, or the sweep-through print — would be a different lead, not a revival of this one.
Direction information itselfCONFIRMED but sub-scaleWith-trend beats counter-trend in every one of three OOS exit configurations, by +0.06 to +0.11R. That is real and it is about the size of the round trip (0.060R). Keep as a prior, do not trade it alone.
The oracle ceilingFINDING — carry it forwardThe $9,610 is a hindsight number. A perfect late boarder reaches $5,094 (53%); a deployable one reaches $1,910–$2,286 (20–24%); 13% of runs are over before any honest trigger fires.

There is no LIVE candidate from this phase, and I am saying so plainly. The one stone I would call still unturned is selection by expected SIZE — the census's own greenfield work found that boarding only fires whose move is ≥120pt pays +$69.38/trade and passes the whole battery, and this study never tested a size predictor at the board moment. That is the next attempt, and it does not need a new data source; it needs a different question asked of the same tape.

11. THE SHADOW BLOCK — AND TWO THINGS THAT MUST BE BUILT FIRST

⚠ This cannot be pasted in as-is. I checked the shadow book's fields against the rule and found two genuine blockers. Both are small, but shipping around either one would record a different strategy under this name — which is exactly how rider_w5 came to be quoted at +$19.29 while making −$28.84.

  1. gate_board cannot express a wrapping clock window. It tests hh_lo <= utc_hour < hh_hi, which is never true for 21:00→07:00. Needs one line: inw = (hh_lo <= h < hh_hi) if hh_lo < hh_hi else (h >= hh_lo or h < hh_hi).
  2. ShadowVariant has an atr_max but no atr_min. The rule is a band, and both edges carry weight (§3). An arm shipped with only the ceiling is a different arm. Needs one field, defaulted to 0.0 so nothing existing changes.
  3. Note on ER. ShadowVariant.er_min reads ER30, not the entry window's ER. Substituting ER30 flips this rule's sign on the held-out sample (§6), so the arm must gate on the 10-minute ER. Either add er_win_min to the gate params or accept that an er_min arm is testing a different hypothesis and label it as such.

With those three in place:

ShadowVariant("board_overnight_band", "board",

              # SEPARATION that generated the idea did NOT reproduce. Random-time placebo inside

Its router rule, in the router's own vocabulary
ARM board_overnight_band when, and only when, all four are true at the tick: 1. the clock is between 21:00 and 07:00 UTC; 2. the router's own ATR meter reads 11.0 to 16.0 points (this is the mean 1-min range over 20 minutes — the number the router already prints; it is a band, so bench it above 16 as well as below 11); 3. RUN STATE is RUN or RUN-FADING — the arm is a boarding rule and has no business firing in declared chop; 4. the untradeable meter is clear and the tape is not inside a scheduled gateway window (04:28–05:00Z sits squarely inside this arm's session and hangs with the port open). BENCH it immediately if the ATR meter leaves the band in either direction, and treat a bench here as cheap: the arm's whole thesis is that both edges of the band carry weight. Expectancy on the home regime only (overnight, ATR 11–16, wide exit): +$10.46 a trade on the 236-session generating sample, +$5.34 a trade on the 28-session held-out sample. Take the lower of those as the working expectation, and note that its own strip-best-3 on the held-out sample is −$51 — three trades were the whole thing. This is not a number to size on.
Promotion bar — deliberately set high

Do not promote this to the paper tournament on P&L alone. It needs all four:

  1. 200 shadow trades, including at least one genuinely trending overnight week;
  2. ≥ +0.15R over those trades after stripping its best three;
  3. the daytime control arm (identical rule, 13:00–20:00Z) must be materially worse — that is the claim under test, and it is the one that failed to replicate;
  4. the counter-trend control must stay negative. It reversed on the held-out lake, and if it reverses again the arm is measuring noise and should be retired without argument.

I would also add the daytime control arm at the same time. Shadowing the treatment without the control is what produced this week's ambiguity in the first place.

VERDICT

NO RIDER SURVIVES. The pooled, direction-agnostic late-boarding run-catcher DIES AT STEP 3 — THE CAUSAL FILTER — killed by the OUT-OF-SAMPLE LEG: 1,289 trades across 236 untouched sessions for a total of +$14, a 95% confidence interval on expectancy of [−0.204R, +0.246R], and a per-trade result that goes negative on one tick of slippage. The verdict is independently corroborated by the live shadow arm rider_w5, which has taken 51 forward trades since 08-17 for −$1,471 (−$28.84/trade), red on six of seven days and red in every ATR bucket including the candidate's own — rider_w5 is REFUTED and should be retired. Step 1 SUCCEEDED and should be believed: a 5-minute boarding trigger fires inside 62 of 62 sat-out runs at a median 3 minutes late with a median 41 points still ahead, so detection is solved. Step 2's wide-exit thesis is CONFIRMED IN DIRECTION but INSUFFICIENT IN SIZE — a wide stop and a far target reliably make this rider less negative and never make it positive across 42 out-of-sample exit cells. The binding constraint is SELECTION: the same trigger fires 34 times a day and roughly 1 fire in 20 is a run, so the rider risks a 33–48 point stop to collect a median 12–41 points. The honest prize is NOT $9,610 — a perfect late boarder with a cheating exit reaches $5,094 (53%), a deployable one reaches $1,910–$2,286 (20–24%), and 13% of the runs are finished before any honest trigger can see them. The causal result on the census week itself was −$245 across 42 trades while participating in 32 of the 62 runs. ONE lead goes forward: board_overnight_band to SHADOW as an instrumented question (+0.444R on 236 generating sessions, +0.224R held-out, but its daytime and counter-trend controls reverse and its placebo p is 0.097), gated behind two small code changes and a four-part promotion bar. The next attempt needs a SIZE PREDICTOR at the board moment, not more days, not a wider exit, and not a new data source — the L2 book was tested as the selector across 311 fires and 264M rows and returned a clean null (r = −0.009, placebo p = 0.62).

UNCLASS — the biggest bucket NOT RUN THIS WEEK · dossier 2026-08-25

The bucket our own classifier could not name, and had therefore never hunted.

GREENFIELD HUNT — CLUSTER UNCLASS

MNQ · full parquet lake · 5s tape 2026-06-19 → 08-24 (51 sessions) + a 205-session 1-minute leg back to 2025-09-14 · $2.00/point · $1.50 per round trip
THE SHORT VERSION, BEFORE ANY OF THE WORKING

Garrath — I did the three steps in the order you set them. I built a direction-agnostic run-catcher and rode the UNCLASS runs without needing to know why they happened. I swept the exit far wider than the desk has ever run one. I filtered it with a causal rule and placebo-controlled every cut against throwing away the same number of fires at random. Then I routed it. It still lost.

It died on the PLACEBO/SHUFFLE TEST, corroborated by the OUT-OF-SAMPLE LEG. On the biggest independent sample I have — 205 sessions of tape that chose nothing — the real signal makes +$3.54 a trade and the fake signal, taken thirty minutes early with every other rule untouched, makes +$4.44 a trade. On the recent forward leg the real signal makes −$9.58 a trade and the fake one makes +$1.48. When a shifted copy of your signal outperforms your signal on two independent samples, you do not have a signal — and per your judging rule that is the named cause of death, not the 25% win rate, which I have deliberately ignored throughout.

Four things came out of the week that are worth more than the dead rider:

  1. UNCLASS is not a cluster and this is now measured twice, independently. I evaluated the census's own waterfall on every one of the 6,784 minutes of its window. UNCLASS is true on 73.9% of the tape and takes 60.3% of the runs — a lift of 0.82. A label with a lift below 1.0 is not a footprint. It is the null hypothesis with a name tag, and "UNCLASS: 41 runs" reads as a discovery when it means "41 runs happened somewhere in the three-quarters of the week we have no test for."
  2. And it is worse than last week thought: 21 of the 68 labels flip on nothing but where a minute starts. I changed one thing — the phase of the 60-second flow buckets — and 31% of the census's cluster assignments changed. Only 17 of 68 run timestamps are minute-aligned, so this is not a hypothetical.
  3. Last week's survivor was never shipped, and the tape since has buried it. UNCL-RIDER-ASIA went to SHADOW on 2026-08-15 and no arm by that name exists in shadow.db. I replayed it myself. It is now four consecutive red weeks, and the newest week — pure forward tape it has never seen — is −$472 over 16 trades, −$29.51 a trade, 18.8% wins. The drawdown that made it a non-deploy last week did not recover; it deepened.
  4. The prize is not $5,840. A boarder that fires inside every UNCLASS run and then exits at the exact top of each move with no costs at all reaches $3,239 — 55%. Put an honest stop on it and bank half the excursion and it is $1,592, 27%. Two thirds of the headline is a close-to-close number that no late entry can ever collect.

The full ledger of every attempt — thirteen named candidates, none of them quietly dropped — is at the bottom, along with the two things I do want to carry forward, both of which are router instruments rather than gates.

1. ★ INTERROGATE THE LABEL FIRST. This outranks anything built on top of it.

Your standing rule, and it changes the whole question. run_census.cluster() is a four-branch waterfall and UNCLASS is the else clause:

amp > 0.30 %                 -> VOL-EXPANSION
13 <= hour < 15              -> OPEN/NEWS
otherwise                    -> UNCLASS

Across the whole tick-covered lake — 49,064 minutes, ten times the sample — it is the same picture: UNCLASS 75.4%, OPEN/NEWS 4.9%, a flow event on 18.0%, VOL-EXPANSION 1.7%.

UNCLASS is true on three quarters of the tape and is UNDER-represented among the runs. That is the whole finding and it outranks every candidate in this document. Last week's number was 74.9% / lift 0.76; mine is 73.9% / lift 0.82 on a different week with a re-derived implementation. Two independent measurements a week apart landing in the same place is about as settled as this desk gets.

And the label is decided by where a minute starts

This is new, and it is worse than the "13% of assignments" figure last week reported, because I isolated the cause instead of estimating it. I changed one thing — the phase of the 60-second flow buckets, wall-clock instead of anchored to each run's own timestamp — and left everything else byte-identical.

The census slides its 15-minute window by array index, not by clock, so where the 5s tape has holes the two drift apart and the run lands at :10, :25, :55 past. Nearly a third of this week's cluster assignments are decided by an arbitrary implementation choice nobody made on purpose.

This is the part that matters for the hunt. I measured the 41 members against the whole tape's distribution, at the run's first minute:

The UNCLASS runs are, at the moment they begin, statistically indistinguishable from a random minute of tape. Their ATR sits below the all-tape median. Their volume is on it. Their efficiency is below it. And you cannot even call the direction — 22 continuation, 19 reversal.

That is not a failure of the census; it is the definition. The other three branches are the tests that find footprints, so the residue is by construction the runs with no footprint. Hunting for a footprint inside UNCLASS is a category error. Which is exactly why your instruction to RIDE first rather than classify first is the right one, and why I did not stop here.

2. STEP ONE — RIDE FIRST. Board it late, and measure what is left.

The rule is deliberately dumb and direction-agnostic: at each completed one-minute bar take the net move over the trailing W minutes; if it is at least k × ATR20, board it in whichever direction the move went. No prediction, no classification.

STEP 1 PASSES, unambiguously. A five-minute boarding trigger gets inside 40 of the 41 runs at a median 3.3 minutes late with a median 31 points / 2.57 ATRs still ahead. Boarding is not the problem and never was. On gold it was 19 minutes in with 80% left; on MNQ it is three minutes in with two and a half ATRs left, which is better.

The trouble is in the right-hand column. That same trigger fires 137 times a day. After the cooldown of actually being in a trade it settles to about 27 entries a day at k=2.0, or 5 a day at k=2.5 with the filter of §4 on. The gap has never been detection. It is selection.

7. THE DIAGNOSIS — which half of the rule was ever doing anything?

The shifted placebo beating the real signal has a specific meaning worth chasing: efficiency is persistent, so a signal taken 30 minutes early still lands on trending tape. So I decomposed it.

armyear leg (205 sessions)recent 5s lake (51 sessions)
A thrust trigger + ER ≥ 0.40 (the candidate)n=1,246 · +$3.54/trn=267 · +$20.72/tr
B same, signal shifted 30 minn=725 · +$4.44/trn=192 · +$15.03/tr
C NO trigger at all — ER ≥ 0.40, direction = sign of the 30-min moven=2,326 · +$3.05/trn=541 · −$6.13/tr
D arm C with the direction flippedn=2,970 · −$2.55/trn=702 · −$0.62/tr
E arm C without the ER gate (every minute)n=5,205 · +$0.05/trn=1,193 · −$1.31/tr
F thrust trigger, NO ER gaten=3,238 · −$3.40/trn=916 · +$3.90/tr

The two legs give opposite answers. On the year leg the thrust trigger is worthless (F is negative) and the ER regime is everything (C ≈ A ≈ B, and D is its clean mirror). On the recent leg the ER regime alone loses money (C is negative) and the trigger is what earns (F positive). Neither component is stable, and a rule whose own decomposition inverts between two samples is measuring the sample, not the market.

Cumulatively: ≥55pt +$56.43/tr, ≥70pt +$65.50, ≥90pt +$77.27, ≥120pt +$109.81. The size threshold is real and it is around 130 points on MNQ — below that the runs pay for themselves and nothing more; above it they carry the entire book.

But that is the PRIZE, not a RULE, and here is why. The rider cannot know the run's eventual size at the moment it boards. The obvious counter-argument is that it can: ATR at board time correlates +0.719 with eventual run size in points, and the 5-minute move correlates +0.851. Those numbers are a scale artefact and I nearly filed them as a finding. Run size is measured in points and so is volatility, so a loud day produces big runs by arithmetic. Normalise the run size by the ATR at board time and the correlations collapse:

The only surviving read is the thrust size expressed in ATRs, at r=+0.48 — and that is already the k parameter, whose sweep in §5 shows no usable gradient. There is a size at which these runs are worth catching. There is no instrument on this desk that identifies it at board time.

Big-moves-caught on the frozen census week: UNCL-RIDE-ER boards 14 of the 41 UNCLASS runs, and its trades on that week are n=33, −$209, −$6.33 a trade.

  • STEP-REPRICE — 5-minute volume ≥ 1.5× the trailing-hour median but |flow z| < 1. Volume arrives and aggression does not: a two-sided repricing, not a sweep. This is the one shape with a genuinely distinctive signature and it is 10 runs / $1,465.
  • GRIND-CONT — the run continues the previous 30-minute drift and ER30 ≥ 0.20. On below-baseline volume, which is what makes it a grind rather than a thrust.
  • DRIFT-VOID — volume below baseline (< 0.95×) and ATR < 12pt. Price walks on nothing.
  • TURN — everything else: a reversal on ordinary volume. Still the biggest half at 19 runs, and still genuinely featureless.

The instrument we would actually need

The binding constraint is named precisely in §8: a SIZE PREDICTOR at board time, in ATR units. Every board-time read we own — ATR, volume, efficiency, thrust size, and (per last week's L2 work, which I did not re-dig) depth imbalance — correlates with a run's eventual size in ATRs at r ≤ 0.13, except thrust-in-ATRs at +0.48, which is already a swept parameter with no gradient. Until something answers "given the volatility, is this going to be a 3-ATR move or a 12-ATR move", this rider risks a 2-ATR stop to collect a median 2.57 ATRs and the arithmetic never closes. That is a missing instrument, not a failed strategy, and it is what the next attempt should go and build.

VERDICT

VERDICT: THE UNCLASS RIDER DID NOT SURVIVE. It was BUILT (a direction-agnostic late boarder that gets inside 40 of the 41 runs at a median 3.3 minutes late with 2.57 ATRs still ahead), RIDDEN (exit swept stop 1.0–4.0×ATR against target 2–16×ATR and caps 30 min–12 h, finding a real 10×ATR target ridge that holds across every stop width), FILTERED (eight causal cuts each placebo-controlled against discarding the same NUMBER of fires at random; ER30 ≥ 0.40 beat its placebo at p = 0.006 and the thin-volume, volume-confirm, loud-tape and looser-ER cuts all failed theirs and are named in the ledger), and ROUTED (arm/bench rules written in the live router's ER / ATR / session vocabulary) — your order of work, in your order — and it STILL LOST. THE TEST THAT KILLED IT IS THE PLACEBO / SHUFFLE TEST, corroborated by the OUT-OF-SAMPLE LEG: on 205 untouched sessions the real signal makes +$3.54 a trade and the SAME rule taken thirty minutes early makes +$4.44, with ten trades out of 1,246 carrying the whole result and only 45% of sessions green; on the 11-session forward leg the real signal makes −$9.58 a trade and the shifted fake makes +$1.48. The family kill is stronger than the single cell: across 137 configurations with usable n on both independent legs, 13% are positive on both against a 12% chance rate, so no setting of this rider replicates any better than a coin. THE LABEL ITSELF IS THE PHASE'S PRIMARY FINDING AND IT IS REFUTED AS A FOOTPRINT — UNCLASS is true on 73.9% of the census window and 75.4% of the whole lake, takes 60.3% of the runs for a LIFT OF 0.82, its members sit ON the all-tape median for ATR (11.65 vs 12.31), volume (1.06 vs 1.02) and efficiency (0.153 vs 0.163), their direction is a 22/19 coin flip, and 21 of the 68 cluster assignments change on nothing but where a sixty-second bucket starts — rename it UNTESTED and report it as coverage. THE BANNED VERDICT IS NOT BEING USED: these runs ARE boardable (40/41) and I have NAMED four shapes (TURN 19, STEP-REPRICE 10, DRIFT-VOID 6, GRIND-CONT 6) for next week's census. The reason they cannot be ridden for money is priced, not asserted: the $5,840 headline is worth $3,239 to a cheating oracle and $1,592 to an honest late board, 57% of fires never become a run, and the size threshold at which a boarded run becomes properly tradeable is ~130 POINTS on MNQ (+$126.56/trade above it versus −$16.12 in the 55–70pt band) — which is a PRIZE and not a RULE, because every board-time instrument we own correlates with eventual run size in ATR units at r ≤ 0.13 once the volatility scale artefact is removed (the tempting +0.72 ATR and +0.85 thrust correlations are scale, and in ATR units they are −0.22 and +0.13). SEPARATELY AND IMPORTANTLY: last week's survivor UNCL-RIDER-ASIA was sent to SHADOW and NEVER SHIPPED — no arm of that name exists in shadow.db — and replayed forward it is REFUTED by four consecutive red ISO weeks (−$2.93, −$15.90, −$36.46, −$38.08), with the pure forward week since 08-17 at −$472 over 16 trades (−$29.51/trade, 18.8% wins); it also boards only 3 of this week's 41 runs and was never an answer to this bucket. TWO THINGS GO FORWARD, both ROUTER INSTRUMENTS rather than gates: BENCH 07:00–13:00Z for any late-boarding rider (red on all three legs including n=373), and SHADOW the ER30 arm-meter with its own control arm (+$3.54 vs −$3.40 a trade on 3,238 untouched trades, but reversing on the last eleven sessions — that reversal is the one cheap question left). THE NEXT ATTEMPT NEEDS A BOARD-TIME SIZE PREDICTOR IN ATR UNITS, not more days, not a wider exit, and not a new cluster label.

0. THE SHORT VERSION, BEFORE ANY OF THE MONEY

Garrath — I was sent to invent a new entry that catches the runs we sat out in the OPEN/NEWS bucket. I built nine, killed all nine, and the thing that killed them is not any one of them.

The order below is the order of importance, not the order I did the work in.

#findingone line
1The label was fixed on 08-15, and the fix worked — but only halfwayOPEN/NEWS is no longer if 13<=hour<15 checked first. It is now the residual: the 13–15Z clock minus a flow event minus a vol-expansion. It went from 100% → 58.7% of its own window. It is still true on the majority of the tape it covers.
2★ Its non-clock content is ANTI-predictiveP(run) is 3.427% on the bare 13–15Z clock and 3.158% on the labelled subset. The two footprint tests strip out 51 of 111 in-window runs and keep the lower-density half. Label lift over the bare clock = 0.92×. Deleting the footprint tests would make the bucket a better predictor than leaving them in.
3★★ The bucket is defined by the ABSENCE of evidenceA run is OPEN/NEWS because no flow footprint and no amplitude footprint was found. Hunting a footprint inside a bucket built from footprint-failures is close to self-defeating, and it dictated where I looked: only channels cluster() never reads — price structure, raw volume, and L2.
4Nine gates, nine gravesORB30, COILBRK, PULSE, PULSE-13h, FADE1, RNGX60, VWRC, OAB, MOMBRK, BOOKLEAN. Every one reported below by name with its stats and its cause of death. Best survivor-on-paper was MOMBRK at +$32.87/trade over 52 trades.
5★★★ THE KILL: a gate with NO TRIGGER AT ALL beats every gate I built"Enter at 13:05Z every day, direction = sign of the last 15 minutes, stop 0.5×U, hold 30 min" — no signal, no arm, no condition — books +$47.29/trade over 26 trades. That is double the best triggered candidate. Every candidate on this page sits inside the noise band of a control that contains no information.
6The window cannot settle the questionPULSE's t-statistic is 1.30. Day-block bootstrap 95% CI [−$4.14, +$26.27]. To get a ±$10/trade confidence interval needs 561 trades ≈ 79 trading days. We have 27.
7★ The size threshold IS the deliverable, and it is ~120ptExpectancy by realised 30-min follow-through: <+20pt → −$38/tr · +60…+120pt → −$4.10/tr · ≥+120pt → +$184.75/tr. Below ~120pt of follow-through the fee and the stop eat everything. 30.8% of armed events cleared it; break-even needed 19.2%.
8Detection has a real footprint; direction does not — and the footprint's honest n is ELEVENTrade-count z-score separates ≥200pt runs at AUC 0.848, rising monotonically from 0.623 at 55pt. But on non-overlapping 30-min blocks the armed sample is n=11, 54.5% ±29.4pp. The AUC is real; the sample behind it is not big enough to trade.
9PULSE and its exact mirror catch the same 6 of the 10 sat-out runsContinuation catches 6/10 for +$150; the direction-reversed twin catches the same 6/10 for +$46. Catching a run is trivial. Getting the side right is the entire problem, and neither does.
10A censoring recommendation, freeVOL-EXPANSION — the label the census barely uses — has 4.18× run lift on 1.95% of the tape, the best of any cluster. OPEN/NEWS has 2.85× on 5.20%. If a bucket is going to route a hunt, that is the one worth widening.

VERDICT (full statement in §12): NULL. Nothing ships, not even to shadow. Cause of death for the section: the trigger-free NULL-CLOCK control (§9) and the day-block bootstrap (§10). Cause of death for the two leaders individually: strip-the-best-trades and the OOS leg. The deliverable is the ~120pt size threshold (§8) and the label finding (§1–2).

1. ★ INTERROGATING THE LABEL FIRST

The brief says to check the cluster label's base rate before trusting anything built on top of it, and that a label true on most of the tape is noise, not a footprint — and that this finding outranks any signal built on top. I did it first. It changed where I was allowed to look.

1.1 What the label is now

Last year's version of this page found OPEN/NEWS was literally if 13 <= hour < 15 checked before every footprint test. That has been fixed. From scripts/run_census.py:78-84:

def cluster(hour, flow, mv, amp, fz=None):
    if flow is not None and fz is not None and abs(fz) >= FLOW_Z:
        return "FLOW-LED" if (flow > 0) == (mv > 0) else "VACUUM"
    if amp is not None and amp > 0.30:
        return "VOL-EXPANSION"
    if 13 <= hour < 15:
        return "OPEN/NEWS"          # no footprint, but the densest window — say so
    return "UNCLASS"

The clock now goes last. OPEN/NEWS is a residual, and the full predicate is a conjunction:

13:00 ≤ hour < 15:00 UTC AND |flow z| < 1 (no aggressor-imbalance event in the prior 60s) AND amp ≤ 0.30 (prior-5-min hi-lo ≤ 0.30% of price)

That is a materially different object from a clock, and the docstring's own claim — that the window is worth keeping as a fallback — is testable. So I tested it.

1.2 Base rate — measured on ALL bars, not on runs

I re-implemented the census's run detector and its three feature functions (flow_at, flow_z_at, amp) against the full parquet lake at 5s — 438,253 bars, 2026-07-16 → 2026-08-21 — and scored the label on every 60s-step 15-minute window, run or not. 36,507 windows.

clusterwindows% of taperuns (≥1.5×ATR)P(run)lift vs 1.109% base
UNCLASS28,00776.72%2400.857%0.77×
FLOW-LED2,9888.18%331.104%1.00×
VACUUM2,9017.95%391.344%1.21×
OPEN/NEWS1,9005.20%603.158%2.85×
VOL-EXPANSION7111.95%334.641%4.18×

Two things fall straight out.

First: the label is true on the majority of its own window. 3,239 windows sit inside 13:00–15:00Z; 1,900 of them (58.66%) wear the label. The 08-15 fix took it from 100% of its window to 59% of its window. That is progress, and it is not enough to call it a footprint — a coin that lands heads 59% of the time inside its own domain is still mostly describing the domain.

Second — and this is the one that matters:

slice of 13–15ZwindowsrunsP(run)lift vs base
the bare clock, everything in 13–15Z3,2391113.427%3.09×
OPEN/NEWS (clock ∧ flow-quiet ∧ amp-quiet)1,900603.158%2.85×
what the label throws away (in-window, has a footprint)1,339513.809%3.43×
★ The label's lift OVER the bare clock is 0.921×.

The two footprint tests take a 3.427%-dense window, remove 41% of it, and keep the less dense half. The bit of the label that is not a clock is not merely uninformative — it is mildly negatively informative. Everything OPEN/NEWS knows about where runs happen, it knows because of the clock.

1.3 Is that an artefact of the pre-tick era?

The lake's ticks start 2026-07-24; before that flow_z_at returns None and the flow test cannot fire, so 07-16…07-23 windows fall through to the clock by default and could be inflating the label. Split it:

erawindows13–15Z P(run)OPEN/NEWS P(run)label lift over clocklabel share of its window
ALL LAKE 07-16→08-2136,5073.427%3.158%0.921×58.66%
TICK ERA 07-24→08-2128,3493.373%3.190%0.946×53.49%

Same answer both ways. In the tick era the label covers 53% of its own window and still returns 0.946× the bare clock's lift. Not an artefact.

1.4 Which of the two footprint tests is doing it

amp > 0.30 is true on only 3.04% of all windows — it barely bites. |fz| ≥ 1 is true on 16.13%. So essentially all of the subtraction is the flow test, and essentially all of the anti-lift is the flow test removing in-window runs that did have a flow footprint and were, on the evidence, slightly more likely to be runs than the ones left behind.

That is not a bug in cluster() — it is doing exactly what it says, routing footprinted runs to FLOW-LED/VACUUM so they reach the hunts that can use them. It is a warning about this bucket: what is left is, by construction, the runs for which the census's two instruments found nothing.

1.5 ★★ What that forces on the hunt

This is the structural point of the whole section, and I want it stated plainly before any gate:

OPEN/NEWS is a bucket defined by the absence of evidence. A run lands here because aggressor flow was unremarkable in the 60 seconds before it and the prior five minutes were not unusually wide. Any signal I build that uses aggressor flow or pre-run amplitude would, if it worked, have relabelled the run out of the bucket. The only channels that can legitimately catch an OPEN/NEWS run are the ones cluster() never reads: - price structure (ranges, levels, VWAP, momentum) — never read; - raw volume / trade count — never read (flow is the net signed aggressor sum; a two-sided auction has huge volume and ~zero net flow, and the label cannot tell it from a dead tape); - L2 book — the census measures book_depletion() and prints it, but cluster() never receives it. Free channel. - cross-asset — out of scope for this section.

Those three are exactly what §4–§7 test, in that order. Nothing here is a flow gate, deliberately.

1.6 A free recommendation for the census

VOL-EXPANSION covers 1.95% of the tape at 4.18× run lift — the highest of any cluster, better than OPEN/NEWS's 2.85× on 5.20%, and it is the label the census currently produces least often (1 run in the frozen week, 33 across the lake). It is checked second, so a run that also has a flow footprint never reaches it. If a bucket is going to route next quarter's hunt, that is the one with the sharpest edge per unit of tape, and its amp > 0.30 threshold — true on 3.04% of tape — is worth sweeping. Not my brief; recorded because I measured it.

2.2 Why I did not backtest on ten runs

Ten runs over five days cannot support a robustness battery, and capture.db — which is what the census reads — is a 5-trading-day rolling window. Anything I fit on it would be fit on the sample. So the hunt runs on the full parquet lake:

[lake] MNQ 5s bars: 438,253 rows, 2026-07-16 00:00 → 2026-08-21 20:59 UTC
       27 trading days · typical 15-min range = 44.2pt · run threshold = 1.5× = 66.4pt
       405 runs ≥ threshold · 60 of them OPEN/NEWS

The lake's threshold (66.4pt) is stricter than the frozen week's (55pt) because the lake's typical 15-min range is wider (44.2 vs 37pt). I kept the census's own arithmetic rather than pinning the number, so the run definition is the census's definition on every day it is applied to.

60 OPEN/NEWS runs on 26 of 27 days — 32 UP, 28 DN, 32 in hour 13 and 28 in hour 14, sizes 68pt to 234pt. No minute-of-hour concentration at all (the busiest single minute has 3 of 60, and 13:30 — the cash open itself — has 2). Whatever this bucket is, it is not a news-release footprint.

2.3 The unit and the costs
  • U = 44.0pt — median 15-min hi-lo range, computed causally (trailing 24h rolling median), so no config knows the future. This is the census's own "typical 15-min range" statistic.
  • $2.00 / point (MNQ; MGC is $10 and is not in this section).
  • $1.50 per ROUND TRIP. Grepped the harness before reuse per the contract: engine.py: TICK, VPP, FEE = 0.25, 2.00, 1.50 and net = gross - FEE charged once per trade. Not $5 (which would have killed every marginal candidate on a fee 3.3× too high), not per side.
  • 1 tick (0.25pt) adverse slippage on every stop-entry and every stop-exit.
  • Pessimistic intrabar: within a 5s bar the stop is checked before the target. A bar that touches both is scored a loss.
2.4 Tick-honesty audit of the fills

The harness runs on 5s OHLC, so I audited the fills against the tick tape (memory: "a wrong-instrument tape PASSES the stop-width sweep" — consistency is not correctness).

No off-tape fills, no all-stop degeneracy, right instrument.

3. WHAT THE TAPE ACTUALLY TELLS YOU BEFORE A RUN

Before inventing anything I measured what is knowable. Per the memory "census pre-run stats are a picker artefact", every discriminator below is measured on the unselected population — every 60s-step window whose forward 15-min move clears the threshold — not on the keep-strongest-deduped run list, which shifts these statistics badly.

3.1 Size is visible. Direction is not.

and the crudest possible direction rule — does the run continue the last 15 minutes? — agrees on 569 of 1,049 in-window runs (54.2%), against a 53.4% base rate on all in-window windows. 0.8 percentage points.

Two consequences I obeyed for the rest of the page:

  1. sq_5_30 = 0.532 refutes the coil-break idea before it is built. There is no compression footprint ahead of these runs. I built COILBRK anyway (§4.2) because a refuted idea with an empty grave is worth less than a refuted idea with a measured one — and it produced one trade at the tight setting, which is itself the answer.
  2. A directional gate cannot be armed on a 0.55-AUC direction call. The only honest shape is to let the tape choose the side — a two-sided stop-entry — or to accept a 54% momentum coin. Both are tested.

The brief says to escalate — full sat-out set, then top-25, then top-15 — because narrowing may reveal a footprint the marginal runs wash out. The clean way to do that with enough n is to sweep the size threshold itself. 13–15Z, tick era, unselected windows:

3.3 ★★ …and the honest n behind that footprint is ELEVEN

Those AUCs are computed on 60s-step windows carrying a 15–30 minute forward horizon. They overlap by ~95%. An n of 2,520 is not 2,520 observations; it is roughly 84 independent 30-minute blocks over 27 days. So I recomputed the headline claim on non-overlapping blocks:

P(30-min move in the momentum direction ≥ X), 13–15Z, one observation per non-overlapping 30-minute block, n=84 blocks:

Xall blocksnt_z ≥ 1.5 blockslift
80pt19.0% (n=84)54.5% (n=11, ±29.4pp 95% CI)2.86×
120pt10.7% (n=84)54.5% (n=11, ±29.4pp)5.09×
150pt8.3% (n=84)45.5% (n=11, ±29.4pp)5.45×
The volume footprint is real, it is large, and its independent sample size is eleven. A 95% confidence interval of ±29 percentage points around a 54% hit rate spans 25%–84%. That is not a footprint you can size a position on; it is a hypothesis that needs a quarter of tape.

For completeness, the same measurement on the raw overlapping 5s bars (n=30,169 in-window, 7,441 armed) gives 15.6% → 27.8% at X=120 — a 1.78× lift. Both numbers are in this report because the gap between them is the finding. Anyone quoting "n=7,441" off this study is quoting 5-second bars, not observations.

4.1 ORB30 — pre-open range break — −$26.98/tr after strip-3

Take the 13:00–13:30Z range (the half-hour into the US cash open), rest a buy-stop 1 tick above and a sell-stop 1 tick below, first touch wins, other cancelled. 27 events, 27 triggers — it fires every single day, which is at least a well-specified gate. Raw +$15.50/tr looks alive. Top 3 trades are 255% of the net — strip them and it is −$26.98/tr; strip 5 and every remaining trade is a full stop. 5 winners out of 27. Cause of death: strip-the-best-trades.

4.2 COILBRK — compression break — 1 trade at the setting the theory wanted

Arm when the 15-min range is ≤ q×U, then two-sided break. §3.1 predicted this would fail (sq_5_30 AUC 0.532) and it failed in the most literal way available:

q15m range must be undereventstrades$/trade
0.4017.6pt11−46.00
0.5022.0pt55−46.00
0.6026.4pt139+54.72
0.7533.0pt3223+30.15

The 13:00–15:00Z window essentially never coils. To get a usable n you must relax the compression test until it stops meaning compression (q=0.75 is a 33pt 15-minute range — barely below the 44pt median). And at q=0.60 the whole $492.50 is three trades (156% of net; strip-3 = −$46.00, i.e. every survivor is a stop) and the long side loses on every one of its trades while the short side makes $105/tr — n=9 split 2/7. Cause of death: n, and parameter sweep — the edge exists only where the compression test has been relaxed into meaninglessness.

4.3 PULSE — 1-minute impulse continuation

Trigger: a 1-minute close-to-close move ≥ k×U inside 13–15Z. Direction = the impulse's sign. Entry: stop order 1 tick beyond that minute's extreme. This is the largest-n candidate on the page and got the fullest battery — §5.

4.4 FADE1 — the exact mirror — −$13.05/tr

Identical trigger, direction reversed, market entry. −$13.05/tr over 211. Not a failure so much as a control that passed: PULSE's +$11.35 and FADE1's −$13.05 are close to symmetric around −$1.50 of fee, which says the two are genuine mirrors and the harness is not manufacturing money from the entry mechanics. That matters — it means PULSE's direction rule is doing something. §5.4 shows it is not doing enough.

4.5 RNGX60 — 60-minute structure break — −$12.02/tr

Two-sided break of the trailing 60-minute high/low. 216 events, 81 triggers. Negative raw, negative at every strip, negative on both sides. Cause of death: negative expectancy, unconditionally. By 13:00Z the 60-minute extremes are the overnight range's edges, and MNQ spends the US open chopping across them.

4.6 VWRC — session-VWAP cross — −$8.59/tr

Enter in the direction of a cross back through the running session VWAP. 42 events, 41 trades, −$8.59/tr, negative both sides, −$24.46 after strip-3. d_vwap had already scored AUC 0.494 for direction in §3.1 — a coin. Cause of death: negative expectancy; predicted by the direction AUC.

4.7 OAB — volume-ignition two-sided break — no parameter plateau

The first gate built deliberately on the §1.5 orthogonal channel. Arm when raw 1-minute volume z ≥ V and |flow z| < 1 — a two-sided auction: heavy trade, balanced aggression, exactly the state the census's net-flow instrument is blind to. Then a two-sided break of the 5-minute range.

The arm itself is real (§3, and lift 1.66× at vol_z>2.5 even restricted to flow-quiet minutes). The gate is not. 192-cell sweep over V ∈ {1.0,1.5,2.0,2.5} × wait ∈ {1,2,3,5} min × stop ∈ {0.375,0.5,0.75}U × target ∈ {0.75,1.0,1.5,None}U:

overall mean $/trade across all 192 cells: -5.15    fraction of cells positive: 0.234

mean $/trade by arm strength × trigger window
 vz \ wait     1min    2min    3min    5min
 1.0          -2.26   -2.57   -6.50   -4.90
 1.5         -10.32   -7.69   -7.82   -5.05
 2.0         -11.89   -6.84  -10.75   -6.00
 2.5          -5.23   +2.55   -1.47   +4.29     <- the only positive row, n=24..30 trades

77% of the surface is negative, and the positive corner is the corner where n collapses to 24–30 trades. V=2.0 is negative in all four wait cells; V=2.5 flips positive. Adjacent parameter cells flip sign. Cause of death: parameter sweep — no plateau; edge appears only as n collapses. That is the curve-fit tell named in the brief.

4.8 MOMBRK — trade-count arm + momentum-direction break

The best-scoring gate I built. Full battery in §6.

4.9 BOOKLEAN — L2 imbalance — full L2 null in §7

9 trades. Reported in the table for completeness; the channel-level result in §7 is the finding.

5. PULSE — the largest-n candidate, killed

Spec (as it would ship):

GATE pulse_open
  SESSION      13:00 <= UTC hour < 15:00
  TRIGGER      |close[t] - close[t-60s]| >= 0.30 x U          (U = 44.0pt, causal 24h median 15m range)
  DIRECTION    d = sign(close[t] - close[t-60s])

  COSTS        1 tick slippage in and out; $1.50 per round trip

time cap5m10m15m20m30m40m60m90m
$/trade+0.70−7.91+11.16+22.19+32.87+41.26+50.92+51.51

It rises essentially monotonically with hold length (with a sign flip at 10m). That is not "an exit rule works", that is "hold longer, capture more of whatever the tape did". A gate whose P&L is a monotone function of how long you stay in is not an entry edge; it is exposure.

The long/short split is the one that should worry us most: MNQ fell −318pt over the sample and −542pt of that accrued inside 13:00–15:00Z, so the long side is not being paid by drift — it is being paid against drift, on 101 trades, while the short side in a falling tape returns $1.13/trade. That asymmetry has no mechanism behind it. It is the signature of a handful of large long winners.

5.4 ★ The placebo — and a correction to how I first ran it

The brief's test: shift the signal series, keep every other rule; if a fake signal books most of the money, the real one is not the edge.

I initially ran this with shifts in both directions and I was wrong to. A negative shift feeds the gate the impulse that happens 5 minutes in the future — that is not a placebo, it is a look-ahead oracle. Both directions are reported below, correctly labelled, because the look-ahead leg is a useful harness check (it must beat the real signal; if it did not, the harness would already be leaking).

−30m−15m−5mREAL+5m+10m+15m+30m+60m
look-aheadlook-aheadlook-aheadstalestalestalestalestale
PULSE 13–15Z+8.05+4.57+30.32+11.35−12.57+8.14−3.46+6.45+8.21
PULSE-13h+10.16+18.40+48.45+23.09−9.51+20.76+18.81+23.95+18.47
  • Harness check: the −5m look-ahead oracle books +$30.32 vs the real +$11.35 (and +$48.45 vs +$23.09 on the 13h variant). The harness is not leaking — knowing the future is worth ~2.7×, as it should be.
  • PULSE 13–15Z: stale placebos average +$1.35/tr = 12% of real, 0 of 5 beat it. Placebo passes.
  • PULSE-13h: stale placebos average +$14.50/tr = 63% of real, and the +30m stale signal books +$23.95 — more than the real signal's +$23.09. Placebo FAILS.

A signal whose 30-minute-stale copy earns as much as it does is not a trigger. It is a slow-moving state variable being read at an arbitrary moment.

§8's regime work shows PULSE's money is entirely in the first hour: 13:00–14:00Z +$23.09/tr (n=95, +$2,194) vs 14:00–15:00Z −$0.28/tr (n=96, −$27). So I ran the battery on the home segment as its own candidate.

6. MOMBRK — the best number on the page, killed hardest

Built directly on §3.2's finding: nt_z is the strongest size discriminator and it strengthens with run size. So: arm on trade-count z, take the momentum side, break-entry.

GATE mombrk_open
  SESSION      13:00 <= UTC hour < 15:00
  ARM          nt_z >= 1.5      (1-min trade COUNT vs trailing 120 non-overlapping 1-min buckets)
  DIRECTION    d = sign(close[t] - close[t-15min])
  ENTRY        resting STOP 1 tick beyond the 5-minute extreme on side d; valid 3 minutes
  STOP         0.5 x U (22pt)      EXIT  time cap 30 min      COOLDOWN 15 min

Base: n=52, net +$1,709, +$32.87/trade, win 23.1%.

Swapping the arm column barely matters (nt_z +32.87, vol_z +24.02, netflow_z +30.98) — the three are near-collinear busy-tape meters, which is the §5.4 point again: this is a state, not a trigger.

6.3 ★ Why leave-one-day-out passed and should not have reassured anyone

All 21 LODO folds are positive. Two days carry 97% of the P&L. Both statements are true at once, and that is a property of the test, not of the gate: with 21 days and 2 money days, removing one day always leaves the other. LODO with k money days cannot fail until you leave k days out. I therefore ran leave-two-out — 210 folds — and the worst fold (drop 07-27 and 07-31 together) collapses to +$1.19/trade, i.e. break-even.

That is worth carrying forward as a rule: quote the number of profitable days alongside any LODO result. 7-up/14-down with a passing LODO is a warning, not a clearance.

Cause of death (MOMBRK): strip-the-best-trades (+$32.87 → +$4.02 at strip-3, −$11.37 at strip-5; top 3 trades are 88.5% of net) and the OOS leg (−$16.50/trade). Confirmed by the day distribution: 7 winning days out of 21, two of which are 97% of the money.

7. THE L2 CHANNEL — a clean null, and one inverted surprise

The book is the one channel cluster() genuinely cannot see (§1.5): run_census.py computes book_depletion() and prints it in the book column, but never passes it to cluster(). Per the data contract, capture.db.book is MNQ-only and event-driven at 41ms — correct for this section — and I read it from the lake (data/tape/book/MNQ/, 2026-07-31 → 08-24, so 16 trading days inside the study window, not 27).

Aggregated to per-minute 3-deep and 10-deep bid/ask size, restricted to 13:00–15:00Z, n=22,979 5s bars:

featurewhat it should predictAUC
imb3 = (bid₃−ask₃)/(bid₃+ask₃)direction of the next 15 min0.508
imb10direction of the next 15 min0.496
imb3direction of the next 30 min0.509
`imb3` (magnitude of the lean)size,fwd15≥ 66pt0.442
depth_z (3-deep size z)size,fwd30≥ 120pt0.557
depth3 (raw 3-deep total size)size,fwd30≥ 120pt0.285

Book LEAN is a coin. 0.508 and 0.496 are as close to nothing as this measurement gets, and the gate built on it (BOOKLEAN, §4.9) produced 9 trades — the threshold that gives a meaningful lean almost never fires inside the US open. On non-overlapping 30-minute blocks in the book era (n=64), |imb3| ≥ 0.1 occurs 4 times and ≥ 0.2 once. There is no sample here.

But depth3 at AUC 0.285 is not nothing — it is inverted. Read the other way, a THIN 3-deep book predicts a ≥120pt move at AUC 0.715, which is better than volume-z (0.674) and better than any book lean measure by a mile. That is the same message as §3.2 from a third instrument: the tape tells you how big, never which way. And like nt_z it is a state variable — thin books cluster in time — so it inherits the same §5.4 problem and I did not build a gate on it.

Cause of death (BOOKLEAN): n=9. Cause of death (the L2 direction channel): AUC 0.508 — no directional information at any depth or horizon.

8. ★ THE SIZE THRESHOLD — this is the deliverable

The brief: report the size-threshold at which a footprint becomes tradeable, if any — that IS the finding. Here it is, three ways.

8.1 The money threshold: ~120pt of follow-through

MOMBRK's 52 trades, bucketed by the realised 30-minute move in the traded direction:

realised follow-throughtrades% of eventsnet $$/trade
≤ −60pt (went hard against)1426.9%−644.0−46.00
−60 … −20pt611.5%−276.0−46.00
−20 … +20pt (nothing happened)917.3%−346.0−38.44
+20 … +60pt23.8%+39.5+19.75
+60 … +120pt59.6%−20.5−4.10
≥ +120pt1630.8%+2,956.0+184.75
A move of +60 to +120 points in your favour still loses money. −$4.10/trade. The 22pt stop gets tagged on the way, or the 30-minute cap arrives before the move does, or the $1.50 and the two ticks of slippage take the rest. Only follow-through beyond ~120pt pays, and when it does it pays +$184.75.

The arithmetic that makes this a rule rather than an observation: with +$184.75 on a hit and −$44 on a miss, break-even hit rate = 44/(184.75+44) = 19.2%. MOMBRK's arm delivered 30.8%. That 11.6-point margin is the entire edge — and §6 shows it does not survive strip-3 or OOS.

This lands on the same number as the desk's existing greenfield finding — "the size threshold is 120pt; ≥120pt boarding pays +$69.38/tr" — from a completely independent cluster and a different harness. Two independent studies converging on ~120pt on MNQ is the most durable thing on this page.

8.2 The detection threshold: a footprint appears above ~120pt, sharpens above 200pt

From §3.2: nt_z AUC runs 0.623 (55pt) → 0.638 (66) → 0.662 (80) → 0.678 (100) → 0.681 (120) → 0.718 (150) → 0.848 (200). The curve is gentle to 120 and steep after 150. The escalation the brief asked for did reveal a footprint that the marginal runs wash out — and it is in the volume channel, not the price channel (rng_30m is flat at 0.62 across the whole range).

8.3 The threshold that matters most: ~11 independent observations

§3.3. On non-overlapping blocks, the ≥120pt armed sample is n=11 at 54.5% ±29.4pp. So:

The tradeable size threshold on MNQ in this window is ≈120pt of 30-minute follow-through. The footprint that predicts it is real (trade-count z, AUC 0.68 at 120pt rising to 0.85 at 200pt). The sample behind that footprint is eleven independent observations, and eleven is not enough to arm a gate on. The instrument we need is not a new measurement — it is more tape.
9. ★★★ THE CONTROL THAT KILLS THE WHOLE SECTION

Every candidate that scored well shared three ingredients: the 13:00–15:00Z window, a momentum-derived direction, and a ~30-minute hold. So I stripped out the only remaining ingredient — the trigger — and ran what is left.

NULL-CLOCK: no arm, no signal, no condition of any kind.
  Enter at a FIXED clock time every trading day.
  Direction = sign(close - close[15 min ago]).   Stop 0.5xU.   Hold 30 min.   Market entry.

13:05Z26+1,229.5+47.2934.6

13:45Z27−125.0−4.6314.8

A gate with no information in it books +$47.29/trade — double the best triggered candidate on this page (PULSE-13h, +$23.09) and 44% more than MOMBRK (+$32.87).

And the same trigger-free rule swings from +$47.29 to −$13.46 purely on which minute of the hour you pick it, across 26–27 trades each. Same rule. Same direction logic. Same stop. Same hold. Twenty-five minutes apart.

For scale, the coin-flip floor: hold the 13:05Z entry times fixed and replace the momentum direction with a fair coin, 100 draws → mean +$2.05/tr, sd $15.21, p95 +$23.70. So the momentum direction rule is worth something (+$47 vs +$2 is about 3 sd) — but p95 of pure noise is +$23.70, which is above PULSE-13h's +$23.09 and within touching distance of MOMBRK's +$32.87.

Every candidate on this page lives inside the noise band of a control that contains no information. That is not a statement about any one gate. It is a statement about what 27 trading days of a two-hour window can and cannot resolve.

11. DID ANYTHING CATCH THE TEN RUNS?

Against the ten sat-out OPEN/NEWS runs of the frozen census (§2.1), ceiling $1,768. Counted as caught if the gate opened a correctly-signed position between 5 minutes before and 15 minutes after the run's start:

That single line is the cluster's whole character. Something fires into these runs reliably — a 1-minute impulse of ≥0.30×U happens near 6 of the 10 — so detection is not the problem. But a gate and its perfect mirror both "catch" 60% of them, and the better of the two converts 8.5% of the ceiling. The run is there; the side is a coin; the money is in neither.

Across the whole lake, MOMBRK caught 17 of the 60 OPEN/NEWS runs (28%) for +$884, and 7 of the 23 that were ≥120pt for +$921 — essentially all of its run-money is in the ≥120pt runs, which is §8.1 restated on the run set rather than the trade set.

12. REGIME SEGMENTATION AND THE ROUTER

The backtest discipline forbids scoring a static config across the whole tape. Regimes are tagged causally per bar: ATR percentile-rank (trailing 2 days) × efficiency ratio over 30 minutes, in the router's own vocabulary.

A bug I fixed mid-study, reported because it would have silently deleted two regimes. My first ER summed 1-minute absolute changes at 5-second spacing — 360 overlapping legs — inflating the path ~12× and driving every ER to ~0.03. Under that ER, clean-trend and building did not exist anywhere in 13–15Z, and the regime table showed only the three chop buckets. Fixed to sum non-overlapping legs (median ER-30m now 0.167). Every regime number below is post-fix.

13–15Z bar counts: building 12,987 · violent-whipsaw 8,679 · dead-chop 8,505 · normal-chop 3,927 · clean-trend 2,575 · trend-thin 2,201.

12.1 What the regime table actually says

The time-of-day split is far stronger than the regime split. PULSE is +$23.09/tr in 13:00–14:00Z and −$0.28/tr in 14:00–15:00Z; MOMBRK is +$51.14 and −$43.90. Within the first hour, every regime except trend-thin is positive; within the second, four of six are negative. Whatever this is, it is a first-hour-of-the-US-cash-session effect, not a volatility-regime effect.

And the regime cells that look best are the ones with no sample: normal-chop 13h is +$157/trade on 4 trades; clean-trend 13h is 6 trades. Those are not home segments, they are anecdotes. The only regime cell with both a decent n and a decent number is dead-chop 13h, +$63.53 on 17 trades — and §9 has already shown that a no-trigger rule entering at 13:05Z makes +$47.29 on 26 trades, so even that cell is not clear of the null.

12.2 ★ The router rule — stated for something that did not survive

A gate that is only viable behind a router condition we cannot yet measure is a finding, not a failure. Nothing here is viable, but the honest statement of what a survivor would need is:

# WOULD-BE ROUTER RULE — NOT FOR DEPLOYMENT. No candidate in this section earned it.
ARM   pulse_open  WHEN  session == US_OPEN
                   AND  13:00 <= utc_hour < 14:00          # the SECOND hour is where it dies
                   AND  regime IN (dead-chop, normal-chop, clean-trend)   # n = 17 / 4 / 6 — NOT a sample
                   AND  nt_z(1min, 120-bucket) >= 1.5      # the size footprint, AUC 0.68 at 120pt
BENCH pulse_open  WHEN  utc_hour >= 14:00
                   OR   regime == trend-thin
                   OR   untradeable_meter == TRUE

Two of those four arm conditions rest on 4 and 6 trades respectively. The router condition we cannot yet measure is not an instrument — it is sample size. We have every input this rule needs (nt_z is computable from ticks in one query, ER and ATR-rank already exist in the router's vocabulary, and the session split is free). What we do not have is 79 trading days of it.

If the desk wants this line of enquiry alive, the cheapest useful thing is not another gate: it is to start logging nt_z, depth3 and the realised 30-min follow-through at 13:00–14:00Z every day, so that by December the ≥120pt question has n in the hundreds instead of eleven.

13. WHAT I DID NOT DO, AND WHY

Stated so the absences are not read as findings.

  • No cross-asset (MGC) leg. MGC is $10/point and gets its own invented-fresh gates in gf_MGC (the gold section below); the contract forbids porting an MNQ gate onto gold and this section is MNQ.
  • No V5 archive extension. gaz:v5archive would add MNQ history before 07-16, but the V5→V7 seam has a real tick hole 07-17 → 07-24 (lake.py warns about it explicitly), and every candidate here needs nt_z/vol_z, which need ticks. Extending bars-only would have widened the sample for the price features while leaving the volume features — the only ones that showed a footprint — on the short sample. I judged a clean 27-day tick-complete sample better than a contaminated 40-day one. This is the single biggest thing that could change the answer, and if the seam is ever bridged, §8's eleven observations is the number to re-run first.
  • No walk-forward re-optimisation. With 27 days and a 2-hour window there is not enough tape to split into fit/select/test three ways; the IS/OOS 2-way split in §5–6 is already thin (OOS n=10–36).
  • No book-pressure gate beyond BOOKLEAN. The L2 direction channel measured AUC 0.508 (§7). I did not build further on a coin.
  • The census was not re-run. census_summary.json and census_stdout.txt are read frozen, as instructed. Everything in §1–3 re-implements the census's functions against the lake; it does not re-cut the census's run list.
