15. VERDICT

NOTHING SURVIVED. Nothing ships — not to live, not to shadow.

What killed the two leaders, individually and by name:

  • MOMBRK (+$32.87/trade, n=52) — killed by strip-the-best-trades and the OOS leg. The top 3 of 52 trades are 88.5% of the net; removing them takes +$32.87 to +$4.02, and removing 5 takes it to −$11.37. Out of sample (08-17 → 08-21) it made −$16.50/trade. Seven of twenty-one days were profitable and two of them are 97% of the money. Its leave-one-day-out passed all 21 folds, which is a property of running LODO with two money days, not a clearance.
  • PULSE-13h (+$23.09/trade, n=95) — killed by the placebo/shuffle test, confirmed by strip-5-best and the OOS leg. A copy of the signal delayed by 30 minutes — same window, same direction rule, same stop, same hold, just a stale trigger — books +$23.95/trade, more than the real signal's +$23.09. Stale placebos average 63% of the real signal's money. Strip 5 trades and it is −$1.89. Out of sample it made −$10.82/trade.

What killed the section: §9. A gate containing no signal at all — "enter at 13:05Z, direction = sign of the last 15 minutes, stop 0.5×U, hold 30 minutes" — books +$47.29/trade over 26 trades, double the best gate I built, and the identical rule 25 minutes later books −$13.46. Everything on this page sits inside the noise band of that control. §10 says the same thing in confidence intervals: t = 1.30 and 1.57, bootstrap 95% CIs of [−$4.14, +$26.27] and [−$2.79, +$52.71], and 561 trades ≈ 79 trading days needed to resolve a $10/trade edge in this window. We have 27.

The deliverables, which are not gates:

  1. ★ The cluster label is a clock with an anti-predictive filter bolted on. The 08-15 fix correctly demoted OPEN/NEWS from checked-first to checked-last, taking it from 100% to 58.7% of its own window. But its lift over the bare clock is 0.921× — the flow and amplitude tests remove 41% of the window and keep the less run-dense half. Same answer in the tick era (0.946×). Per the brief's own instruction, this finding outranks every signal on the page. Recommendation: either drop the two footprint tests from the OPEN/NEWS fallback and call it what it is (US-OPEN-WINDOW, 3.09× lift on 8.87% of tape), or route the hunt through VOL-EXPANSION instead — 4.18× lift on 1.95% of tape, the sharpest cluster the census produces and the one it uses least.
  1. ★ The tradeable size threshold is ≈120 points of 30-minute follow-through. Below it the gate loses even when right: +60…+120pt of follow-through still books −$4.10/trade. Above it, +$184.75/trade. Break-even hit rate is 19.2%; the best arm delivered 30.8%. This is the same ~120pt number the desk's independent greenfield work reached from a different cluster with a different harness — the most durable result on this page.
  1. ★ Detection has a real footprint and it is VOLUME, not price; direction has none; and the footprint's honest sample is eleven. Trade-count z separates ≥200pt runs at AUC 0.848, rising monotonically from 0.623 at 55pt, while 30-minute range is flat at 0.62 throughout — so this is not "wide days have wide runs". Direction tops out at AUC 0.55–0.65 and the crude momentum rule agrees with runs 54.2% of the time against a 53.4% base. On non-overlapping 30-minute blocks the armed sample for the ≥120pt claim is n=11 at 54.5% ±29.4pp. And the cluster's own character, in one line: PULSE and its exact mirror catch the same 6 of the 10 sat-out runs. Detection is solved. Selection is not.
  1. A test-design finding worth keeping. Leave-one-day-out cannot fail when k days carry the money and you only remove one. MOMBRK passed 21/21 LODO folds while two of twenty-one days held 97% of its P&L. Always quote profitable-days-out-of-total next to a LODO result, and run leave-two-out when the day distribution is that skewed (MOMBRK's worst leave-two fold: +$1.19/tr).
  1. A harness finding. A signal shifted backwards is a look-ahead oracle, not a placebo. Only forward (stale) shifts are legitimate placebos; the backward shifts belong in the report as a harness leak-check, which this harness passed (look-ahead earns 2.7× the real signal, as it should). Reported because I ran it the wrong way first and it would have produced a false kill.

Full working, every sweep and every null: this file. Tick-honesty audit §2.4 — 40/40 entries and 40/40 exits inside their own bar's tick range, MNQ only, $1.50 per round trip, $2.00 per point.

FLOW-LED — aggressor-driven continuation NOT RUN THIS WEEK · dossier 2026-08-25

Runs the tape pushed. Nine candidates built off the flow print.

GREENFIELD HUNT — cluster FLOW-LED

Full working, all attempts, all graves

MNQ · tick-honest over the full Parquet lake, 2026-07-05 → 2026-08-25 (35 tape days, 45,466,604 ticks) Costs: MNQ $2.00/point, fee $1.50 per round trip, 1 tick (0.25pt) adverse slippage on entry and on every stop.

0. The headline, before any signal

The cluster label is not a footprint. FLOW-LED and VACUUM are a coin flip, and the coin is flipped by the future.

The census assigns FLOW-LED when the prior-60s net aggressor flow is unusual (|flow-z| ≥ 1.0) and its sign agrees with the FORWARD 15-minute move; VACUUM is the identical test with the signs disagreeing. The second half of that definition is only knowable after the run has happened. At the moment a gate would have to fire, both labels look exactly the same.

Measured on 43,982 minute bars of lake tape that carry a valid flow-z and a resolvable +15min close:

testresult
base rate of the flow-event half (|fz| ≥ 1.0) on all bars20.58 %
given a flow event, flow agrees with the next 15 min49.62 % (n = 9,022)
control — bars with |fz| < 1.0, same question49.29 % (n = 34,786)
⇒ information carried by the flow event about direction0.33 percentage points
FLOW-LED base rate on all bars10.21 %
VACUUM base rate on all bars10.37 %

The flow event does not meet the "true on most of the tape" failure mode — 20.6 % is a real filter, and the 2026-08-01 z-score fix that replaced abs(flow) > 50 (66.5 % of bars) did its job. The label fails for a different and worse reason: the filter fires on a fifth of the tape and then splits that fifth into two almost exactly equal halves on a coin toss. FLOW-LED vs VACUUM is not two tape behaviours, it is one population cut by its own outcome.

Directly:

E[fwd15 in the flow's direction]
  |fz|>=1.0   -0.299 pt   n=9,053   t = -0.61
  |fz|>=1.5   +0.408 pt   n=4,594   t = +0.54
  |fz|>=2.0   +0.067 pt   n=2,655   t = +0.06
  |fz|>=2.5   -0.029 pt   n=1,660   t = -0.02

Zero at every threshold, with the sign wandering. The census's own 4 FLOW-LED / 13 flow-event runs (30.8 % agreement) is not evidence of a contrarian tape: against the lake's 49.62 % null, P(≤4 of 13) = 0.139. Expected FLOW-LED among 68 census runs = 9.0, observed 4; expected VACUUM = 9.6, observed 9. Both inside noise. The cluster has n=4 because 68 runs is too few to populate a 10 %-base-rate label, not because the tape did something.

0b. Flow does predict magnitude — but that is a volume channel wearing a flow costume
conditionE|fwd15|vs base
base (all bars)26.70 pt1.000×
|fz| ≥ 1.533.64 pt1.260×
|fz| ≥ 3.041.73 pt1.563×
|volume-z| ≥ 2.041.75 pt1.564×
flow unusual, volume ORDINARY (|fz|≥1.5 & |volz|<1.0)25.70 pt0.963×
volume unusual, flow BALANCED (|volz|≥1.5 & |fz|<0.5)32.56 pt1.220×

Strip the volume out of the flow event and the magnitude lift vanishes entirely (0.963× — below base). Strip the flow out of the volume event and the lift survives (1.220×). The census's flow column is a volume proxy. Net aggressor imbalance adds nothing over "a lot traded".

That is the strongest statement this section can make, and it outranks everything below.

1. Method

Everything derives from ticks in gazbot7.lake (2026-07-05 → 08-25; the documented 07-18→07-23 V5/V7 seam is absent, weekends absent — 35 tape days, 44,847 minute buckets). capture.db was never touched: it holds 5 trading days and would have shrunk the sample 7×.

  • No lookahead. A minute row at ts covers ticks [ts, ts+60), so it is only known at ts+60. Every entry is stamped ets = ts+60. ATR is .shift(1)-ed off closed 5-min bars; every z-score uses closed='left' on a trailing 120-min window with ≥30 buckets, exactly the census recipe.
  • Contiguity guard. er30/brk30 use .shift(30); across a weekend or the V5/V7 seam that silently compares two different tapes. 97.5 % of rows pass the guard; the rest are dropped, not used. (The two largest "minute moves" in the tape, 408.5pt and 295.75pt, are both 00:00:00 Monday weekend gaps — they are excluded by this guard, not traded.)
  • Tick-honest exits. Entry at the first print ≥ ets, filled 1 tick adverse. Stops fill 1 tick adverse to the stop price; targets fill at the limit; the time stop fills at the print. Stop is tested before target on every print (the pessimistic ordering). One position at a time.
  • Regimes keyed on ATR level + ER + range-break, not the clock: DEAD-CHOP (atr_rel<0.70 & er30<0.30), VIOLENT-WHIPSAW (atr_rel≥1.6 & er30<0.35), CLEAN-TREND (er30≥0.55), BUILDING (0.35≤er30<0.55), NORMAL-CHOP otherwise. Sessions ASIA / LONDON / US / LATE.
Engine integrity check (run before believing any positive number)

Random-direction entries on the identical row set, five seeds:

seed 0  n=221  $ -5.27/tr      seed 3  n=222  $-13.59/tr
seed 1  n=219  $-11.05/tr      seed 4  n=224  $ -2.24/tr
seed 2  n=220  $ -1.30/tr

All negative, as a healthy engine must be — a coin flip pays the fee and the slippage. There is no drift bug manufacturing the numbers below.

6. The residue — and why it is not this section's survivor

The flow-free half of FL-4 is the only thing on this page with a pulse after the battery:

plain 30-min range-break, ≥0.5×ATR, in high ATR (atr_rel ≥ 1.6). No flow term whatsoever. n = 491, net +$2,929.68, $/tr +$5.97, win 50.5 %, 5/5 walk-forward folds profitable, 18/68 census runs caught for +$1,323.80. Exit mix: TIME 285 (+$20.6/tr) · TGT 102 (+$150.8/tr) · STOP 158 (−$112.9/tr).

I am not reporting this as a survivor, for three reasons, and the operator should treat it as a lead for the structure-break phase rather than a gate:

  1. Its block-bootstrap 95 % CI is [−2.12, +14.36] — it straddles zero exactly as FL-4 did.
  2. Its own IS/OOS split is +$10.38 → +$1.04/tr. Positive, but $1.04 is a third of the fee.
  3. Its US-session leg, which is 483 of its 491 trades, goes IS +$13.64 → OOS −$2.15.

More importantly: it is not a flow gate, and it is not this cluster. Reporting a breakout gate as the FLOW-LED cluster's finding would be the exact error the census made — attaching a flow name to something the flow had no part in.

Router rule, if it is ever picked up by another phase (stated in live-router vocabulary so it is falsifiable): ARM when atr_rel ≥ 1.4 (ATR-14 on 5-min bars vs its trailing 24h median) and session = US; BENCH otherwise; no ER condition — the ER term was measured to be worth 4 cents. Note that atr_rel is not currently an instrument the live router reads — the router's LAST HR ATR is a mean range, not the true-range ATR-14 this is keyed to, so arming on the router's existing number would arm on the wrong measurement. That is the instrument we would need to build first.

7. What would have to be true for this cluster to be worth revisiting

The FLOW-LED hypothesis is not refuted in principle — it is refuted with the instrument we have. The census's flow is a 60-second net-aggressor count from ticks.aggressor, and §0b shows it is a volume proxy. Three measurements would make it a fresh question rather than a repeat of this one:

  1. Resting-liquidity flow, not print flow. capture.db.book is 41 ms event-driven and MNQ-only. The question worth asking is not "who crossed the spread" but "did the far side get pulled" — that is a book measurement, and it is the one the census's book column already gestures at.
  2. Flow at a level, not flow in a clock minute. A fixed 60-second bucket splits a single institutional order across two buckets and merges two unrelated ones. Volume-clock or order-imbalance-at-price buckets are the standard fix, and the tick data supports both.
  3. A run population large enough to populate a 10 %-base-rate label. 68 runs cannot; the lake's 5,066 bars at ≥55pt can. Any future cluster work should be labelled on the lake and only illustrated on the week's census.

VERDICT

NOT SURVIVED. No FLOW-LED entry signal reached a tradeable expectancy. Nine candidates were built and all nine are dead: FL-2/3/6/7 on negative expectancy at the blanket screen, FL-1 on the OOS leg, FL-5 and FL-8 on strip-the-3-best (with FL-8 also beaten outright by its own placebo), FL-9 on the parameter sweep, and the last survivor FL-4 flow_ignition on the PLACEBO/SHUFFLE TEST — empirical p = 0.150, with 6 of 40 time-shifted fake flow series matching or beating it and the best fake (+$16.25/tr) beating the real signal (+$12.18/tr) outright — corroborated by a paired ablation in which the flow term's contribution inverts from +$39.43/tr in-sample to −$11.71/tr out-of-sample, and by 3/5 walk-forward folds against 5/5 for the same gate with the flow term deleted.

There is no size threshold at which a FLOW-LED footprint becomes tradeable. On the predictor side every flow-z bar from 1.0 to 4.0 is positive in-sample and negative out-of-sample. On the outcome side, flow agreement with the run is 48.4 %–53.7 % from 55pt to 200pt and never departs from a coin flip by as much as one sigma.

★ The finding that outranks all of the above: the cluster label itself is not a footprint. The flow-event filter fires on 20.58 % of all bars and then splits that fifth into FLOW-LED (10.21 % of tape) and VACUUM (10.37 %) on a 49.62 % coin toss — 0.33 percentage points of directional information versus the |fz|<1 control. Whatever lift the flow event carries is a magnitude lift, and that lift is entirely a volume proxy: flow unusual with volume ordinary gives 0.963× base E|fwd15| (no lift at all), while volume unusual with flow balanced gives 1.220×. The census's flow column measures how much traded, not who was buying. Recommendation: stop splitting the run census into FLOW-LED/VACUUM. The two labels are one population cut by its own outcome, and the week's 4-vs-9 split is noise (expected 9.0 vs 9.6; P(≤4 of 13) = 0.139 against the lake null).

VACUUM — the snap-back / stop-run NOT RUN THIS WEEK · dossier 2026-08-22

Runs that moved AGAINST the tape.

GREENFIELD HUNT — cluster VACUUM (census 2026-08-16 → 2026-08-21)

The job. Ignore every gate we own. Invent a brand-new entry signal that shows up for the runs the census filed under VACUUM, spec it mechanically, backtest it tick-honest over the full Parquet lake at the true $1.50 round-trip fee, escalate to the biggest runs if it fails, and try hard to kill it. Working below; every attempt is named, including the graves.

THE THREE ANSWERS, IN ORDER OF HOW MUCH THEY MATTER

1. ★ The VACUUM label is not a footprint — and this week I found where it comes from. Last Friday's section established that the label is a coin flip. This week's larger sample (33 trading days, 43.2M ticks, 42,143 tape-minutes) confirms that and goes one step further. The flow event the label is built on fires on 20.41% of every minute of tape we own. Given that event, the direction test comes up "VACUUM" 49.90% of the time — against 49.91% on minutes where no flow event happened at all. That is a −0.01pp difference. But the census still reports VACUUM on 15.7% of its runs, well above the 10.2% base rate, and I traced the whole of that excess to a selection artefact in run_census.py's own run-picker. The picker takes every 60s-slid 15-min window over threshold and dedupes "keep-strongest", so the surviving minute is by construction the local extremum of the move. Rebuilding that picker on the lake: the prior-5-minute price direction agrees with the run 48.66% of the time on unselected big minutes and 22.55% after the dedup — a −26.11pp shift created purely by the selection rule. The census's own 65 sat-out runs read 24.6%, matching the rebuilt picker almost exactly. Push the VACUUM condition through the same three populations and it goes 10.45% → 14.01% → 21.87%. VACUUM is the name the census gives to the fact that it picked a local bottom.

2. Detection is real, it is size-graded, and it is the answer to the size-threshold question — but direction is a coin flip and I could not break it. A volume-z / ATR-expansion detector separates the biggest runs from ordinary tape at AUC 0.69 (p<0.0001) on the 113 lake-wide runs of 120pt+, rising monotonically from 0.557 at 55–70pt. On the census's own top-15 the volume-z AUC is 0.730, p=0.0004. Turned into a bracket gate (VAC-IGN-BRK) it catches 9 of the 65 sat-out runs and 5 of the top-15 on only 48 fires in the census week — 3.6× the random-fire baseline. And it still cannot be traded, because the sign-flip control earns exactly as much as the signal (+$3.08 vs +$3.21 per trade). We can see the runs coming. We cannot tell which way they go.

3. Last week's shadow candidate failed its forward test, and last week's one open stone is now closed. VAC-ABS reproduced to the dollar on the in-sample leg (+$24.04/tr vs the +$24.91 reported) and then lost −$529.50 over 27 trades (−$19.61/tr) on the five fresh days. Its strip-5 is −$427. It is dead, not shadowed. And the L2 far-side-depletion discriminator that last week's report nominated as "the one stone still unturned" is refuted: on 21 days and 246.9M book rows it predicts the next 15 minutes' direction at 49.44% ±2.52pp.

⚠ A method note that changed every headline in this section. My first pass let overlapping entries run concurrently. Five separate shorts booked the same 2026-07-31 impulse and were worth $3.9k of a $10.3k headline. A live gate takes one lot and cannot re-enter until flat. Everything below is scored one position at a time; where the unconstrained number is shown it is labelled as such and is never the verdict. Under the honest accounting VAC-IGN-BRK falls from +$10,316 / +$15.49 per trade to +$911.55 / +$3.21 — 91% of the apparent edge was one impulse counted five times.

1. What the census labelled, and what the label is made of

scripts/run_census.py::cluster() calls a run VACUUM when, in the 60 seconds before it starts, net aggressor flow was unusual for that moment (|z| ≥ 1.0 against the trailing two hours of the same statistic) and pointed the opposite way to the move that followed. Plain English: the tape was full of buyers and then price fell.

This week: 11 VACUUM runs of 70, of which 9 sat out, carrying $1,595 of 1-lot hindsight ceiling out of the week's $9,986 total sat-out ceiling.

Read the definition again. The label uses the forward move to decide the label. You cannot know a minute is VACUUM until you already know where price went for the next fifteen minutes. That is fine for a taxonomy and fatal for a trigger. The only thing knowable in advance is the flow z-score, so that is what I tested — and then I tested the label itself.

One minute in five is a "real flow event", and knowing that tells you nothing whatsoever about which way the next fifteen minutes go. VACUUM is a normal flow minute with a coin landed on it.

2.1 So why does the census see 15.7% and not 10.2%?

Because the run-picker selects local extrema. stage5_artifact.py rebuilds the picker on the lake — every minute with |fwd15| ≥ 55pt, then "keep-strongest" dedup at 15-min spacing — and compares three populations:

Verification: the census's own 65 sat-out runs read 24.6% on prior-5-min agreement — the rebuilt picker says 22.55%, the unselected tape says 48.66%. The picker, not the tape, is doing the work.

The disagreement rate goes 50.4% → 51.8% → 76.9% purely by selecting local extrema. The VACUUM cluster does not describe a state of the tape. It describes the census's dedup rule. ★ This finding outranks every signal in this document and is the reason none of them was ever going to work as specified.

What this does not say. The census is not broken as a taxonomy — "where was the money and did we show up" is answered correctly, and the sat-out ceiling of $9,986 stands. What is unsafe is treating a cluster name as a hunting ground, and any pre-run price-path statistic quoted off the run list.

3.1 The three mechanical specs, for the record

VAC-SNAP — invented here, refuted here. On completed 1-min bars: cumflow5 = Σ netflow over the last 5 bars; z5 = its z-score against the trailing 2h of the same statistic. ARM when z5 ≥ +1.5 (buyers) and the 5-bar price change is ≤ 0.35 × ATR(1m,14) — heavy one-sided aggression that failed to move price. TRIGGER within 10 bars when a bar closes below the arming window's low → SHORT (mirror for sellers absorbed → LONG on a close above the window high). ENTRY first tick after that bar closes. STOP 2.0 × ATR(1m,14). EXIT stop or 30-min time-stop.

VAC-IGN-BRK — invented here, the one that detects. volz = z-score of bar volume against the trailing 120 bars; atr_ratio = ATR(1m,14) averaged over 5 bars ÷ over 60 bars. ARM when volz ≥ 2.0 and atr_ratio ≥ 1.15. TRIGGER within 10 bars when a bar closes outside the 5-bar range — above the high → LONG, below the low → SHORT. Non-directional by construction: the tape picks the side, the gate only picks the moment. ENTRY first tick after that bar closes. STOP 1.5 × ATR(1m,14). EXIT stop or 30-min time-stop.

VAC-ABS — last week's spec, unaltered, forward-tested. |z(netflow)| ≥ 3.0 and |close − prev close| ≤ 2.75pt → fade the aggressors. Stop 2.0 × ATR, 30-min time-stop.

7. ★ THE ROUTER — what would be armed, and the honest answer that nothing is

The mandate is explicit that a blanket cross-tape number is a bug and that a surviving gate must come with its home regime and an arm rule in the live router's vocabulary. Nothing survived, so what follows is the segmentation evidence and the rule that would have been written, stated so it is falsifiable rather than aspirational.

The regime split is consistent across all three candidates and is the one genuine policy finding here — every one of them is an ATR-high, US-session animal and every one of them bleeds in low ATR:

VAC-ABSVAC-SNAPVAC-IGN-BRK
ATR low tercile−$5.26/tr (n=33)−$8.10/tr (n=137)−$11.64/tr (n=95)
ATR mid tercile−$5.99/tr (n=31)−$10.09/tr (n=136)+$3.24/tr (n=94)
ATR high tercile+$50.86/tr (n=33)+$20.82/tr (n=137)+$18.03/tr (n=95)
US session 13:00–21:00Z+$51.24/tr (n=26)+$22.89/tr (n=104)+$16.33/tr (n=110)
overnight / pre-open−$0.18/tr (n=71)−$6.57/tr (n=306)−$5.08/tr (n=174)

ER is not a discriminator here, in either direction. Serially, VAC-IGN-BRK books −$0.49/tr in dead chop (ER15 < 0.15, n=83), +$17.85/tr in the 0.15–0.35 middle (n=93) and −$6.55/tr in clean trend (n=108) — a middle bucket carrying the whole of a $911 net across three buckets is noise, not a regime. ⚠ Recorded because it matters: the unconstrained run said +$22.28 in chop and +$13.79 in trend, and that was the overlap-inflated ledger — exactly the number this section warns against quoting.

What is a router finding, and it comes from the detection work in §5 rather than from any backtest: the biggest runs start from chop — ER15 is the only feature measured whose AUC sits below 0.5, and it falls further as the runs get bigger (0.442 on the sat-out 65, 0.403 on the top-15). Every ER-floor arm condition the live router owns is standing gates down at the moment the largest moves begin. That belongs to the router section, not to a gate.

The rule that would have been written, had the sign-flip control not killed it:

ARM vac_ign_brk when ATR(1m,14) ≥ 21.0pt on MNQ and 13:00 ≤ t < 21:00Z. BENCH below 19.0pt (2-point hysteresis, matching the existing 2-mark convention) with a ≥5-minute dwell on the arm side — ATR crossing a bare threshold on a partial bar is exactly the oscillation that produced 20 switch changes for 4 trades on 08-07. No ER condition, for the reason above. Expectancy on that home regime only: +$18.03/trade over 95 trades. Blanket, as context and never as the verdict: +$3.21 over 284.

Do not arm it. The home-regime number is the same number the fade control earns; conditioning on ATR-high selects trades with more range in both directions, and a gate that makes money whichever way you point it is a volatility harvester with a stop, not an edge.

What we would need to measure to make this tradeable. A direction discriminator that is not price, not aggressor flow, and not top-3 book depth — all three are ruled out above at tight error bars. The concrete candidates, in order of how cheaply we could instrument them: (i) full-depth book imbalance beyond level 3, including queue-position and cancel/replace rate — depth.db carries the wide snapshot but at 250ms it cannot see the fleeting quotes capture.db.book does at 41ms, so this needs the 41ms feed widened past level 3, which is an IBKR subscription question, not a code question; (ii) cross-instrument lead-lag — we already capture MGC L1+L2 and MES/M2K depth, and none of this week's work looked at whether gold or the breadth complex turns first; (iii) a trade-size distribution split (large-lot vs small-lot aggressor), which the tick stream already carries in size and which no census or gate on this desk currently uses. (iii) is free and is the one I would run first next Friday.

MGC: deliberately not attempted. The scope is explicit that gold gates are invented fresh, never ported or re-tuned from an MNQ gate, and the VACUUM cluster is a property of the MNQ census. Porting VAC-IGN-BRK to gold would have been the wrong kind of easy number — and at $10.00/point a mis-priced transfer would have looked five times more exciting than it was. Gold is gf_MGC's work, and it is directly below this section.

VERDICT

The VACUUM cluster did NOT survive, and for the second Friday running it was killed by the LABEL itself rather than by a backtest — but this week the mechanism is identified, not just the symptom. The census's flow event fires on 20.41% of every tape-minute we own, and conditional on it firing the VACUUM direction test comes up VACUUM 49.90% of the time against 49.91% on non-event minutes — −0.01pp, inside a ±1.1pp error bar. The apparent excess in the census (15.7% of runs vs a 10.2% base rate) is entirely a selection artefact of run_census.py's keep-strongest run-picker: prior 5-min price direction agrees with the run 48.66% of the time on unselected big moves and 22.55% after the dedup, and the VACUUM rate climbs 10.45% → 14.01% → 21.87% across the same three populations. VACUUM is the name we give to having picked a local bottom. Traded literally (VAC-Z1) it loses −$4,150.79 over 1,768 trades serial, −$32,184 over 8,589 unconstrained.

Four candidates were invented and all four are graves, each with a named cause of death. VAC-SNAP (absorption → structural break, +$370.64 / n=410) — killed by strip-the-3-best (−$1,436) and the OOS leg (−$18.02/tr). VAC-CUMDIV — refuted outright, negative at every threshold. VAC-ABS (last week's shadow candidate, forward-tested unaltered, +$1,319.21 / n=97 / +$13.60 per trade net of $1.50 per round trip) — killed by its OUT-OF-SAMPLE LEG, −$529.50 over 27 trades on the five days it had never seen, confirmed by strip-5 = −$427; it is now RETIRED, not shadowed. VAC-IGN-BRK (the detection bracket, +$911.55 / n=284) — killed by the SIGN-FLIP CONTROL: fading the break earns +$3.08/trade against the signal's +$3.21, so both directions win and it is volatility harvesting, not edge; the parameter surface is a step rather than a plateau and 4 of 15 cells are negative.

The size-threshold question has a real answer this week, and it is a detection threshold, not a tradeability one. Below |move| ≈ 87pt (the top-15 band) three of four detectors are indistinguishable from noise; at and above it all four go significant — volume-z AUC 0.730, p=0.0004 on the census's top-15, rising lake-wide to AUC 0.867 on ATR for the 113 runs of 120pt+. VAC-IGN-BRK converts that into 9 of 65 sat-out runs and 5 of the top-15 caught on 48 fires — 3.6× the random-fire baseline, the first thing in this workstream that demonstrably shows up for the big runs. It is still not a gate, because detection without direction is a coin flip with a stop, and the sign-flip control proves it.

Last week's one open stone is closed: the L2 far-side-depletion discriminator is REFUTED — 49.44% ±2.52pp on unselected 55pt+ moves over 21 days and 246.9M book rows, 49.72% ±0.67pp on all 21,249 book-minutes. Do not revive it at 30 days; the null is not n-limited.

⚠ And one methodological finding that should outlive this section: the first pass of this backtest let overlapping entries run concurrently, and five shorts into the single 2026-07-31 impulse were worth $3.9k of a $10.3k headline. Scored one position at a time — the only way a live gate can trade — VAC-IGN-BRK falls from +$15.49 to +$3.21 per trade. 91% of the apparent edge was one impulse counted five times. Every greenfield harness on this desk should be checked for it.

Dispositions: NOTHING to LIVE. NOTHING to SHADOW. VAC-ABS retired from shadow. Two findings handed onward — (1) the census run-picker's local-extremum artefact, which invalidates every pre-run price-path statistic quoted off the run list and should be fixed or flagged in run_census.py; (2) the biggest runs start from CHOP (ER15 AUC 0.403), so every ER-floor arm condition the router owns is standing gates down at the moment the largest moves begin. The single cheapest next experiment is a large-lot vs small-lot aggressor split — the size field is already in the tick stream and no gate or census on this desk uses it.

GOLD — the MGC greenfield (gf_MGC), and the blocker that did not survive thirty-two days

This section was missing from Rev 1 and it should not have been. The gold phase ran on 2026-08-28 and wrote four artifacts at 23:58Z; the report then shipped with no gold greenfield section at all, while three other places pointed at “gf_MGC” as though it were in the document. Gold is the operator's #1 stated new-instrument priority. Everything below is computed at render time from those artifacts — scripts/friday_v7_gold_section.py.

The gold answer in four lines

1 — The bar-source blocker is DEAD, and it was never the variable. Last cycle's gold section led with “the sign flips on the bar source alone” — +$3.06/trade on lab bars against −$8.96 on production bars — measured on six days. On 32 days both arms are the same sign and both are negative: −$1.21/trade on lab bars (506 trades) and −$0.41/trade on production bars (299). On the 19 days both tapes cover it is −$1.76 against −$0.41. There is no flip at any level.

2 — What the bar source really controls is HOW OFTEN it fires, not how well. The lab's mid-bar arm takes 2,459 raw fires against production's 1,451, and 178 of the lab arm's 506 trades (35.2%) land in minutes where the trade tape printed nothing at all. A mid quote flickers when nobody trades; a trade bar cannot. The lab arm was not reading a better price series — it was admitting a population of dead-tape breaks that cannot be filled.

3 — Activity is the real axis, and it does not survive being fitted. Split by how busy the tape is, the busiest quartile carries everything (production bars: +$27.11/trade in Q4 against −$11.85 in Q1). Fit an activity floor in-sample and it looks superb — +$40.80/trade at floor 40. Apply that same floor FORWARD and it is −$11.92/trade on 12 trades. The floor is a fit, not a filter.

4 — Nothing gold-side goes anywhere near a shadow arm this week, and the cause of death is named. Every arm here is negative pooled, and each one gets worse when its three best trades are removed. That is the strip-the-best-trades test, and failing it is the one result a thin sample can still deliver honestly.

Identical gate (60-minute break, 0.10 ATR margin, obstacle-free hole, 45-minute per-side cooldown), identical exit (3.0 ATR stop behind a 2.0/2.0 chandelier, 480-minute backstop), raced on the same 250 ms quote tape with both legs crossing. The double hole — a break with no obstacle in front of it and no resting support behind it — is positive on BOTH bar sources, which is exactly the agreement the bar-source scare said we could never have. Cause of death: strip-the-best-trades. Both arms go from positive to negative when three trades are removed — from +$921.50 to −$109.00 on lab bars, and from +$468.00 to −$328.50 on production bars. Three trades out of 311 and 154 are the entire result. It also turns negative in F2 on both. Not refuted — a thin sample never is — but nowhere near a shadow arm, and the specific thing it needs is more trades, not more tuning.

GOLD — VERDICT, and what to do about it

Gold is an EMPTY SEAT, not a bleed. There is no live gold gate, so the census ceiling gold prints each week is the size of the opportunity, not money forgone. Nothing here arms, nothing here shadows, and no MNQ gate is ported across — the scope's standing rule that gold gates must be invented fresh is unchanged and is reinforced by G4: the two instruments do not even have the same relationship to their own tape.

What actually moved this week. The bar-source blocker that gated the entire gold programme is gone — retired on 32 days after being raised on 6. That is a real deliverable: the next gold cycle does not have to spend itself reconciling two bar builders. The blocker it is replaced by is smaller and more useful: gold's edge, if it has one, lives in the busiest quartile of the tape, and every attempt so far to express that as a threshold has been a fit. The next experiment is an activity measure chosen a priori and run forward for a stated number of sessions — the same discipline the Open Rider's pre-registered ATR filter is under, applied to gold.

⚠ Honest limits, all of them. 32 days is one summer of one instrument. F2 is three days. The double-hole cell is 311 and 154 trades and dies on three of them. Every figure is a REPLAY on the 250 ms quote tape with both legs crossing — it is the best counterfactual available and it is not a fill. And gold has never traded live on this desk, so nothing here has ever met a real queue.

A proofread pass ran against the first draft of this report and left eight questions open — things the sections had the halves of and never joined, or asked for and did not answer. Each one is answered below from real data, computed for this revision, with the harness named so it can be re-run rather than re-argued. Three of them changed a recommendation on the action card; one of them changed a number the front page leads with. Where the answer is “we still cannot tell”, it says that and says what would settle it.

Q1 The Monday promotion, after the desk's own live haircut

The promotion is a SHADOW number. This desk's standing correction is that live losses run 1.1–3.1× modelled — wider stops slip, fills are worse, and the model's loss is the optimistic end. The report had both halves and never joined them. Joining them: abs_veto_55s's 433 trades are +$13,586.00 of wins against −$8,283.50 of losses, so multiplying only the loss side by λ gives

Loss multiplier λNet$/tradeRead

So the promotion survives the bottom quarter of its own haircut band and nothing above. That is not a reason to cancel it — every promotion this desk has ever made would fail at 3.1× — but it is a reason to size it small and grade it on realised slippage rather than on P&L. The first twenty live fills should be compared against what the shadow said they would be worth; if the realised loss multiple comes in above 1.64×, the arm is a null and not a winner, and you will know that from twenty trades rather than from a quarter's P&L.

★ And the second half of Q1 has a better answer than expected: there is no ATR floor to worry about

The question asked whether the promoted slot runs WITH or WITHOUT an ATR floor, because if it runs with one it is not the arm that made $5,302. It runs without one, and so does the live gate it is promoted into. deciders.py:203: ATR_FLOOR = {"grind_long": 22.0, "capitulation_long": 10.0} — abs_veto_long and abs_veto_short are not in it. And the shadow arm is not a looser trigger either: shadow.py:840 builds abs_veto_55s from {"thr": 1.5, "amp_floor": 0.0004} with confirm_s=55, which is identical to the live slots' own parameters in slot_strategy.py. The promoted arm and the live gate are the same entry.

This also corrects Part 1 §6, which attributed its −$143.61-vs-+$948.50 gap to “the shadow variants carry no ATR floor”. They do not, but neither does the gate. The real difference is that SUPPRESSED-OPEN is logged UPSTREAM of the 55-second veto, so the 65 live intents are the PRE-veto population and the shadow's 45 are POST-veto. The refutation stands and it is now about the right mechanism. §6 has been rewritten.

⚠ Honest note on the shadow's own ATR distribution: entries run 11.3–47.5 with a mean of 16.7, and 377 of 433 trades carrying $4,968.50 of the $5,302.50 sit below ATR 22. That is below grind's floor, not this gate's — but it does mean the arm lives on medium tape, and a future ATR floor anywhere near 20 would delete almost all of it.

Q2 Can the dead band be declined off the ATR meter we already have?

Movement 3 §3 says every precursor we own is an ATR proxy carrying no direction. §7 says the money is in SIZE — 48.2% of entries land in the ±20-point dead band and pay $10 each to find out — and that declining them needs no direction call. Those two findings pointed at each other with nobody in between. Here is the bridge, run on §7's own pooled book with §3's own AUC harness. Bar stated in advance and not moved: AUC ≥ 0.60 means buildable. Harness: scripts/rev2_deadband_classifier.py (2,000 permutations, seed 20260829).

The answer to the question as asked is YES. ATR at entry separates dead-band entries at 0.683 with a permutation p of 0.0005. Low ATR predicts “nothing is going to happen in points”, which is close to a tautology and is exactly why it works.

And §3's finding shows up again, and this time it does not bite. Against an ATR-normalised dead band the same feature reads 0.531 — a coin flip, for the third time in this report. But §7's band is defined in POINTS and the friction is paid in DOLLARS, and dollars are points × $2.00. The desk does not pay its bills in ATR. That is the distinction the two sections needed: §3's collapse is fatal when you want to predict a MOVE, which is scale-free; it is not fatal when you want to predict SIZE IN MONEY.

★ But the money leg FAILS, and the cause of death is named

Detection is not a strategy. Declining the lowest-ATR 48.2% of the book takes it from −$2,813.99 (−$1.64/trade) to +$1,517.61 over 886 trades (+$1.71/trade) — a $4,331 swing and a sign flip with no direction call at all. Then the robustness battery:

TestResultVerdict
Strip the best 3 trades from the kept book+$1,517.61 → −$266.64FAILS — three trades of 886 are the whole result
Walk-forward — fit the cut on the first half (ATR 12.84), apply it to the secondfirst half kept −$2.82/tr (vs −$1.97 unfiltered); second half kept +$7.04/tr (vs −$1.32)FAILS — it loses in the half it was fitted on
Oracle ceiling (decline the TRUE dead band)+$5,715.26 (+$6.39/tr)the ATR rule captures 27% of it

So: BUILD #4 is not closed and it is not promoted. Its own kill criterion said “close it loudly if AUC < 0.60” — the AUC is 0.683, so it is not closed. But the dollar rule dies on strip-best-3, which is this desk's own standing kill test, so it is not built either. It ships as a SHADOW arm with a threshold pre-registered before the data, exactly like the Open Rider's ATR filter: pick the cut a priori, run it forward for a stated number of sessions, and grade it on strip-best-3 and a genuine out-of-sample leg rather than on the swing. A rule that inverts on three trades of 886 is a rule about three trades.

Q3 What to do about the day rider on Monday

Answered in full in Part 1 §3b, which is new in this revision, and on the card as SATURDAY #4 and HOLD #7. The short version, because it is the bigger book and it deserves a straight answer:

  • Keep the no-stop decision. Re-priced on this week's own tape at seven stop widths off the ATR the rider itself froze at entry: on the twelve positions this week actually opened, naked made +$572.50 and every stop width lost money, the best of them at −$617.44. Your 2026-08-20 call wins by $1,189.94 on this week's evidence, not just on the 231 sessions it was taken on.
  • The one trade that argues otherwise is not a stop argument. The 08-21 carry is −$2,149.44 naked against −$34.56 at the tightest stop — and it was carried through a 49-hour CME halt, where no stop can fill. The rule that would have prevented it is the standing flat-by-20:40Z one, and it failed for an unrelated reason.
  • ★ And the real bill is somewhere else entirely. Every rider order this week filled as a split whose residual leg was priced base × (1 ± 0.001), adverse, at a price the tape never printed within ±10 seconds. Twelve such events, 20 of 116 lots, $1,170.50 — against a rider week of −$1,576.94. 74% of the loss is a fill artefact, not a trading decision. That is SATURDAY #4 and it outranks the stop question by a wide margin.

The standing instruction that falls out: re-price the no-stop decision every Friday. It takes one script (scripts/rev2_rider_stop_week.py) and about a minute. The difference between a standing decision and an unwatched one is whether anybody checks it.

★ And the thing worth saying out loud, which the proofread spotted: the two gates measured CLEAN are the two we can say least about. grind_long's whole saving is one Tuesday and capitulation_long is n=5 and negative. The clean half of the sample is the weak half. The argument for the bench was never the dollar figure: it is that every cut points the same way, and that in aligned trend benching is FREE (50 signals, −$0.81 each) — which is the actual case for arming aggressively on a confirmed break, and it does not depend on the magnitude at all.

Q5 “Wait for one trend week” — how long is that wait?

Four recommendations are parked on it: the router timing config, the aligned-vs-chop gap, the two-ratchet, and the BIG-TREND state. Nobody has ever counted how often a trend week happens. Here it is, on every session in the lake from 2026-06-19 to 2026-08-28 — 51 days, 11 ISO weeks — using whole-day efficiency ratio (net move divided by summed path) on the desk's own 22:00Z-to-22:00Z day boundary.

The same threshold on the same tape gives 0, 6, 18, 27 or 34 trend days depending only on the bar size the path is summed over — and the report quotes “ER 0.017–0.032” for this week without saying which. A threshold whose meaning moves by 34 days across a rendering choice cannot gate four recommendations. What IS stable is the ORDERING: 2026-08-04, 2026-07-30, 2026-08-18 and 2026-07-21 are the top four days at every bar size. So the usable definition is a RANK, not a level.

Fixing the definition at 5-minute path, ER ≥ 0.15 (which picks almost exactly the top decile) and counting by week:

Six of eleven weeks contained a trend DAY. Not one contained a trend WEEK. The maximum in any week, across the whole record, is one. So four recommendations are waiting for an event that has never occurred, at a rate of 0.55 trend days per week — and at that rate, ten trend days is eighteen weeks away.

What to do instead — and everything that is queued behind it, in one place

Replace “wait for a trend week” with “accumulate N trend DAYS by a DATE”. A trend day is a day; the shadow arms can collect them one at a time, and the grade happens on the date whether the sample arrived or not — because “we did not get enough” is a result and an open shadow arm with no review date is not.

Q6 capit_loose is 49% of the board's loss and the live gate is armed by cron. Which is it?

Both, and they are not the same mechanism — which is the answer the report owed and did not give.

ArmConfignNet$/fireWin%What it is
capit_looseclimax 2.5 · dom 0.60 · no flip · 1.0R1,038−$16,681.00−$16.0717.2%the config this desk REVERTED on 2026-08-02
capit_live_mirrorthe live gate's own parameters, unbenched352−$5,515.50−$15.6712.5%the honest counterfactual for the live gate
capitulation_long LIVEclimax 2.5 · dom 0.6 · flip=True · 2.0R34+$63.00+$1.8538.2%what the desk actually booked, 07-21 → 08-28

1 — capit_loose is NOT the live mechanism, and Part 2 should stop implying it is. It runs require_flip=False at a 1.0R target. That is precisely the configuration this desk shipped on 2026-08-01 and withdrew on 2026-08-02 after finding the statistic behind it (“78% of bounces reach 1R”) was an MFE measure being used as a win rate — the ordering-correct number was 29%, against a 50% breakeven. slot_strategy.py records the whole autopsy in place. So capit_loose's −$16,681 is not an indictment of the live gate; it is a 1,038-trade gravestone for the config we already rejected, and it is doing its job. Calling it “the only true relegation case on the board” is right, and it should be relegated — but relegating it says nothing about the live gate.

2 — The live gate's own counterfactual is bad, and that IS the case to answer. capit_live_mirror runs the live parameters with no benching: −$15.67 a fire over 352 fires at a 12.5% win rate. The live gate took 34 of those 352 — the 10% the switch file happened to leave armed — and made +$63.00. The live gate's positive record is what BENCHING selected, not what the gate does.

3 — And the +$63.00 is smaller than this week's single win. The gate booked +$148.50 on 2026-08-28 at 14:00Z. Its all-time is +$63.00. So on the other 32 fills of its life it is −$85.50. One trade is more than the whole record.

★ So NOT-AN-ACTION #10 stops being a governance observation and becomes a decision

reactivate_gates.py arms capitulation_long at 22:00Z nightly and the router does not clean it up, so it accounted for the large majority of the desk's armed hours this week by rota rather than by decision. On the evidence above there are exactly two defensible positions and “leave it as it is” is not one of them:

  • Either the router owns it like the other five — remove it from the cron's roster and let the tick arm and bench it on the same criteria. Its unbenched counterfactual loses $15.67 a fire, so leaving the arming decision to a clock is leaving $15.67 a fire to a clock.
  • Or the asymmetry is written down as deliberate, with the reason, in reactivate_gates.py itself — because a carve-out nobody can find the rationale for is indistinguishable from a bug, and this one has produced the week's largest single win, which is the most dangerous way for a bug to behave.

⚠ The honest limit: n=34 live fills over six weeks, and the mirror is a replay rather than a book of fills. Neither number is strong. But the DECISION is not a P&L question — it is about which instrument owns the switch, and that does not need n.

Q7 exhaustion_short — a gate benched pending evidence it can only make while armed

It has been off in gate_switches.env since 2026-08-18 and has not fired since. Two of this report's own instruments point opposite ways on it: Part 2.6 §3.2 prices the UP_OFF rule at +$516 of benched winners over 98 blocked legs, and Part 1 §7 prices its bench at +$442.65 saved over 34 signals but marks it NOT PROVEN because the stop sweep flips at 0.5×. Part 2 §9 asks for 40+ fills on the gate's own exits before the fade-scalp trial can be graded. It cannot collect them while benched. That is a deadlock and the report should have named it as one.

EraWindowDays armedFillsMachine exitsMANUAL_CLAIMNet
A — pre-trial, stop 1.0×ATR07-21 → 08-14151461388−$158.00
B+C — the fade-scalp trial08-17, 08-1821477+$165.50
benched08-19 → 08-280000—

The arithmetic that breaks the deadlock. Era A fired 9.7 fills per armed day. In the trial, 7 of 14 fills (50%) ended on the gate's own exits rather than on your claim button. So 40 machine-exited fills needs about 80 fills, which is about 8.2 armed trading days.

The re-arm condition, stated so it can be executed

Arm exhaustion_short for eight trading days: Monday 2026-08-31 through Tuesday 2026-09-15. Grade on 40 machine-exited fills (MANUAL_CLAIM legs excluded from the grade, counted separately) or that date, whichever comes first. Then decide.

Why the exposure is acceptable, in numbers rather than in nerve. Era A's entire 146-fill history at the OLD config is −$158.00, or −$1.08 a fill; 80 fills at that rate is about −$86. Against that, Part 2.6 prices the UP_OFF bench at +$516 of benched WINNERS this week alone. The expected cost of collecting the sample is roughly one bad hour and it is the only way the trial ever gets graded.

And the alternative is worse than it looks. A gate benched pending evidence it cannot generate is not “parked”; it is retired without a verdict, and next Friday's report will find it in exactly this state again, as this one did. The desk's own standing lesson applies: a lapsed bench is not an arming case — but a bench that makes its own evidence impossible is not a bench either, it is a decision nobody has taken.

⚠ If you would rather not arm it, that is a legitimate answer — but then BUILD #6 and the Part 2 §9 grading request should both be withdrawn rather than carried, because they are asking for something the desk has decided not to produce.

Q8 Part 0's stale date was the fourth instance of this week's pattern. What else is like that?

This report's headline is that instruments fail silently and in the direction of reassurance — a router blind for 3h35m, two nightlies with no timer, two byte-identical shadow arms. Then Part 0 shipped a week stale, inside the report that names the pattern, because AS_OF was a literal. So: a sweep of the report's own generators and the nightly rollups for hard-coded dates and week constants. It took five minutes and it found six more.

File · constantValueVerdict
scripts/fv7_common.py · WEEK_LO / WEEK_HI / DAYS / DAYNAME2026-08-17 → 2026-08-22, and a hard-coded five-day list★ THE LIVE ONE This is LAST week, and it is a shared helper imported by six Friday phase scripts — fv7_p1_live, fv7_p2_shadow, fv7_p26_router, fv7_p15_rehab, fv7_p25_musings, fv7_m2_idle. They were not used this cycle (the phases wrote their own HTML), but they are on disk, they import cleanly, and anyone who reaches for them gets a confident answer about the wrong week with no error. Same failure as Part 0, one import away from half the report.
scripts/abs_veto_sides.py · WEEK02026-07-27CONFIRMED Already caught by Part 2 this cycle: its column headed “this week” is four and a half weeks and reports +$4,069 where the truth is +$948.50. Listed here because it is the same bug, not a separate one.
scripts/friday/progress_page.py · AS_OFwas 2026-08-21FIXED THIS REVISION Now derived from the report week, with a --as-of override, and the page says so in its own closing paragraph.
scripts/friday_v7_build.py · CYCLE_START2026-08-28 22:00ZCORRECT AS A LITERAL It is the definition of “this cycle” and the stale-fragment check is built on it. It must be set per cycle, and if it is forgotten the build says so loudly rather than silently — a stale fragment gets a red dated banner. This is the safe shape.
gf3_*.py, gf4_mgc_barsource.py · IS_END = 2026-08-15 · gf2_mgc_forward.py · SPLIT · gf_mgc_lab.py · OOS_CUT · router_churn.py · CUTOVERvariousCORRECT, AND MUST NOT BE DERIVED These pin an in-sample / out-of-sample boundary or a config change-over. A walk-forward split that moves with the calendar is not a walk-forward split — it leaks. Freezing them is the point.
exit_ladder_lab_v2.py · START · gf_cs_regime.py · START/END · momentum_veto_sweep.py · SINCE · adaptive_r_policy.py · ARCH_ENDvarious 2026-07 datesAGE HARMLESSLY, BUT AGE These are data-availability floors ("the lake starts here", "depth starts here"). They only ever narrow a sample, never mis-date one, so they cannot produce a wrong answer — but gf_cs_regime.py's END = 2026-08-15 silently drops the two most recent weeks from anything that re-runs it.

The rule the sweep suggests, and it is cheap. A date literal is fine when it names an EVENT (a config change, an out-of-sample boundary, the day a feed started) and dangerous when it names NOW (this week, as-of, the current cycle). The two are trivially distinguishable and nothing on this box distinguishes them. One convention would close the whole class: a constant that means “now” is either derived or carries a # EXPIRES: <date> comment that a pre-flight check reads and fails on. This report already has a pre-flight that refuses stale fragments; it has nothing that refuses a stale constant.

★ And the answer to the second half of Q8 — “did anything check the report's own generators?” — is no. Nothing did, until a proofread pass noticed that a chart was missing a week. Every instrument failure this report is proud of finding was found by the report; the report's own instruments were found by reading the report. That is one rung further out and it is not a different problem.
